# How Evert Calderon Uses SuperMoney and Novae at Mesa Group Consulting

## The Short Answer

Evert Calderon is using both **SuperMoney** and **Novae** as commissioned affiliate/fulfillment partners at Mesa Group Consulting. The Miro board is a build/execution roadmap for ten new pages on mesagroupconsulting.com, with each page assigned to whichever affiliate backend supplies its offers, forms, and commission structure. Mesa Group's own published FTC-compliant Affiliate Disclosure explicitly names both companies as partners ([mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure), [mesagroupconsulting.com/disclaimer](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/disclaimer)).

The split follows a clear business logic:

- **SuperMoney** powers the five commodity consumer-lending pages (credit cards, personal loans, auto loan refi, student loan refi, debt consolidation) — high-volume, self-serve, per-qualified-lead traffic.
- **Novae** powers the five higher-ticket, more consultative service pages (debt relief, trust & will, life insurance, business debt relief, business credit) — done-for-you services with per-signup and residual commissions.

---

## What SuperMoney Is

SuperMoney (SuperMoney, LLC; Santa Ana, CA; founded June 18, 2013 by Miron Lulic) is a financial-services comparison marketplace and aggregator — often described as a "KAYAK-like" experience for financial products. It is not a lender or bank ([en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SuperMoney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SuperMoney), [help.supermoney.com/article/50-is-supermoney-a-lender](https://help.supermoney.com/article/50-is-supermoney-a-lender)). The company spans 50+ consumer finance categories, lets users compare offers from many lenders and banks in one place, and provides real-time, pre-qualified loan offers via a single soft-pull form ([supermoney.com/about](https://www.supermoney.com/about), [help.supermoney.com/article/61-what-does-super money-do](https://help.supermoney.com/article/61-what-does-supermoney-do)).

**Company scale and recognition:**
- Bootstrapped (no venture capital).
- $10+ billion in loan requests and ~2 million registered members as of 2023; reached $5B milestone by May 2021 ([supermoney.com press release](https://www.supermoney.com/supermoney-hits-10b-loan-requests-and-1m-members-on-10th-anniversary)).
- Lender partners include Chase, Citi, PNC Bank, Marcus by Goldman Sachs, PenFed Credit Union, LendingClub, Pentagon Federal Credit Union, and dozens more ([supermoney.com/monetize](https://www.supermoney.com/monetize)).
- Inc. 5000 list 2021–2023; Deloitte Technology Fast 500 in 2022; SOC 2 Type II certified.

**How SuperMoney makes money:** commissions from financial institutions when a user takes a product found through the platform, plus app subscriptions and advertising ([help.supermoney.com/article/62-how-does-supermoney-make-money](https://help.supermoney.com/article/62-how-does-supermoney-make-money)).

### SuperMoney's Publisher/Affiliate Program

SuperMoney runs an explicit program for site owners with audiences of credit-challenged consumers who want to monetize that traffic ([supermoney.com/monetize](https://www.supermoney.com/monetize)). Three monetization tools:

1. **Super Links** — tracking links dropped into existing content, plus co-branded pages that monetize even when the product being discussed doesn't pay out directly ([supermoney.com/monetize/super-links](https://www.supermoney.com/monetize/super-links)).
2. **Money Marketplace** — an embeddable comparison widget that lives on the publisher's own site under the publisher's brand ([supermoney.com/monetize/money-marketplace](https://www.supermoney.com/monetize/money-marketplace)).
3. **Pre-Qualification Platform** — lets the publisher offer real financing options to users without sending them off-site, including a rev-share arrangement: *"Many lenders build out their own financial marketplaces entirely powered by SuperMoney's 50+ widgets… SuperMoney actually pays its partners a rev-share of the commissions it receives"* ([supermoney.com/monetize/prequalification-platform](https://www.supermoney.com/monetize/prequalification-platform), [help.supermoney.com/article/33](https://help.supermoney.com/article/33-how-can-i-partner-with-supermoney)).

SuperMoney pitches itself on the fact that it pays **per qualified lead**, not per funded loan — meaning publishers get paid sooner. FlexOffers advertises that the program offers "commissionable direction," high conversion rates from leading lenders, and "some of the highest EPCs [earnings per click] in the space" ([flexoffers.com affiliate listing](https://www.flexoffers.com/affiliate-programs/supermoney-affiliate-program/)).

**Public commission benchmarks** (from third-party affiliate networks; Mesa's own rates are confidential):
- Credit cards: ~$50 commission per approval; CPA offers listed at ~$65; 60–75% rev-share variants ([revshare.so listing](https://www.revshare.so/programs/advertiser/supermoney-credit-cards-0de12e53), [affplus.com listing](https://www.affplus.com/o/supermoney-personal-credit-cards-revshare-us-6)).
- Personal loans: 75% rev-share CPA listings ([affplus.com listing](https://www.affplus.com/o/supermoney-cps-supermoney-personal-loans-desk-mob-us-75)).
- General marketplace: up to 30% per sale via Takeads ([takeads.com listing](https://takeads.com/merchants/supermoney-us/)).

The underlying lender network spans prime to subprime (SoFi, LendingClub, Upgrade, Best Egg, Rocket Loans, OppLoans, NetCredit, Reprise, etc.) — which matters for Evert's credit-repair clientele ([supermoney.com/quotes/personal-loans/own-up](https://www.supermoney.com/quotes/personal-loans/own-up?network=partner&offer_id=1191&aff_id=1145)).

### How Evert Is Using SuperMoney

Mesa Group's affiliate disclosure confirms the relationship verbatim:

> "SuperMoney: Financial product comparison platform offering personal loans, auto loan refinancing, student loan refinancing, debt consolidation loans, and credit card comparisons. When you use SuperMoney through our referral links or secure loans/products, we may receive a commission."
> — [mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure)

This is an exact one-to-one match with the five "supermoney affiliate" entries on his Miro board:
- credit cards
- personal loans
- auto loan refi
- student loan refi
- debt consolidation loan

In practice, Evert has either embedded SuperMoney's widgets on those new pages or used Super Links to send visitors into SuperMoney's pre-qualification engine. The credit cards page is already live and matches this pattern exactly: a card-matching flow ("Pre-qualified offers… Compare 400+ cards… Match based on your credit profile") with a "Powered by" attribution and the disclosure *"Mesa Group Consulting is not a card issuer. We help you compare offers from our partners and may earn a referral fee if you're approved, at no extra cost to you"* ([mesagroupconsulting.com/credit-cards](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/credit-cards)). Every time a referred user fills out a qualifying inquiry on SuperMoney (or, depending on the product vertical, funds a loan or opens a credit card), Mesa Group earns a commission at no extra cost to the consumer.

---

## What Novae Is

Novae (Novae, LLC; 1506 Klondike Road Ste 403, Conyers, GA; founded 2014 by Reco McDaniel McCambry) describes itself as *"a fintech company that provides greater access to credit, capital, and entrepreneurship for consumers and small businesses nationwide, with a particular interest in empowering underserved communities"* ([novaemoney.com/](https://novaemoney.com/), [novaemoney.com/base/compensation-plan](https://novaemoney.com/base/compensation-plan)).

It is a **member of the Direct Selling Association** — i.e., a direct-selling/MLM-style distribution model, not a conventional fintech (the DSA Code of Ethics signatory status is stated in the footer of Novae's product pages, e.g., [novaemoney.com/life-insurance/](https://novaemoney.com/life-insurance/)). Other recognition: Inc. 5000 fastest-growing company 2021–2024; BBB A+ rating; customers in all 50 states plus Puerto Rico.

Key clarification: **Novae is not a lender and does not perform credit repair for clients.** Its own loan page says: *"No, Novae is simply a site that allows prospective borrowers to apply to be pre-qualified or pre-approved for a loan through a network of lenders"* ([novaemoney.com/trsolutions/novae-money-loans](https://novaemoney.com/trsolutions/novae-money-loans)). Its consumer disclaimer adds: *"Novae provides self-directed credit software, credit education and credit monitoring tools. Novae does not work on your credit for you, and no score increase, item removal, approval, funding or timeline is promised… No income is guaranteed, and most participants should not expect substantial income"* ([novaemoney.com/consumers/](https://novaemoney.com/consumers/)).

### Two Layers to Understand

Unlike SuperMoney (a pure aggregator), Novae is two things at once:

**1. A product/technology company.** It builds its own subscription fintech products (myNovaeCredit Monitoring, myNovaeDisputes Manager — an AI-powered credit dispute manager), has its own tax-prep software, and operates LLC formation, vacation-incentive, and grant programs.

**2. An affiliate network / co-brand platform.** It packages third-party services (loans, debt relief, business funding, life insurance through PolicyGenius, wills and trusts through Trust & Will, etc.) so that partners like Mesa Group can either:
- Sell/earn from those services individually as a Novae affiliate, **or**
- Wrap the entire Novae product catalog under their own brand using Novae's "Co-Brand" turnkey website package, marketed as "zero lift, start offering all of the following in-demand financial services" ([start.novaecobrand.com](https://start.novaecobrand.com/), [novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/](https://novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/)).

### The Full Novae Product Catalog (relevant to the Miro board)

| Consumer | Small Business |
|---|---|
| Debt Help (settlement/negotiation, $10k+ debt, 20–48 months) | Business Credit Builder ($995 DIY / $2,495 guided, $50K+ positioning) |
| Credit Cards | Business Funding (offered in all 50 states) |
| Personal Loans | Business Debt Relief/Help |
| Life Insurance (via PolicyGenius) | Business HELOC |
| Tax Preparation | Credit To Cash |
| Savings Accounts | Consumer Financing |
| Auto Loan Refinance | Business Debt Help |
| Student Loan Refinance | Grants & Government Loans |
| myNovaeCredit Monitoring | Free Business Registration (LLC) |
| myNovaeDisputes Manager | Business Essential Services |
| Wills & Trusts (via Trust & Will) | Vacation Incentives Program |
| No-Interest Cash-Advance Loans | |
| Instant Tax Refund | |

Sources: [start.novaecobrand.com](https://start.novaecobrand.com/), [novaemoney.com/base/become-an-affiliate](https://novaemoney.com/base/become-an-affiliate), [novaemoney.com/trsolutions/debt-help](https://novaemoney.com/trsolutions/debt-help), [novaemoney.com/biznestfunding/business-credit](https://novaemoney.com/biznestfunding/business-credit), [novaemoney.com/ericlh/business-funding-programs](https://novaemoney.com/ericlh/business-funding-programs).

**Back-end partnerships confirmed:**
- Life insurance: Novae's page explicitly states *"we've partnered with Policygenius, a trusted leader in the industry… personalized quotes from top insurers"* ([novaemoney.com/life-insurance/](https://novaemoney.com/life-insurance/)).
- Wills/trusts: Novae's "Start a Will" copy references "Trust & Will" by name and offers "attorney support" identical to Trust & Will's own product ([novaemoney.com/kccreditdoc/wills](https://novaemoney.com/kccreditdoc/wills), [novaemoney.com/coo/trusts](https://novaemoney.com/coo/trusts)).

### How the Novae Affiliate Program Works

**Standard affiliate tiers** (enrollment fees vary across sources/time periods, but the structure is consistent):
- **Affiliate Basic** — roughly $199 upfront + $49/mo (direct sales only, no team overrides).
- **Affiliate Pro** (sometimes called "Plus") — roughly $299–$499 upfront + $69–$99/mo (direct sales + team-building; unlocks personal commissions, team override commissions, and rank-advancement bonuses like residual income, monthly bonuses, "luxury car payments," mortgage payments, investment club access, and private stock) ([novaemoney.com/base/become-an-affiliate](https://novaemoney.com/base/become-an-affiliate), [novaemoneytraining.com enrollment agreement PDF](https://novaemoneytraining.com/wp-content/uploads/Affiliate_Enrollment_Agreement.pdf)).

The compensation plan explicitly provides for **override commissions across ten generations** of recruited affiliates. Novae's own income disclosure states the **average participant earned $1,408 in 2023**, with Novae noting some earn less, some more, and "some… fail to achieve a meaningful level of success" ([novaemoney.com/consumers/](https://novaemoney.com/consumers/)).

**Product-level commission benchmarks** (compiled from Novae's published compensation plan, per [behindmlm.com](https://behindmlm.com/mlm-reviews/novae-money-review-financial-services-rebrand-stock-fraud/)):
- Personal Loans / Business Funding / Consumer Financial Products: 35% of third-party commission
- Business Credit Finance Suite: $500/signup ($200 DIY tier)
- Life Insurance: $50/signup
- Will & Trust: $20–$50/signup
- Credit/disputes monitoring: $100/signup
- Debt Help (consumer): 1% per signup; Business Debt Help: 50% per signup
- Co-Brand program: $500–$900 per signup; White Label: $3,000 per signup

A separate **Referral Partner Program** pays **20% of what referred merchants pay, up front and monthly**, plus the option to earn "up to 100 basis points from collective finance volume" ([novaemoney.com/base/financing-referral-partner](https://novaemoney.com/base/financing-referral-partner)).

The **Co-Brand program** is the most likely fit for what the Miro board shows: *"A Curated financial services turn-key web package, powered by Novae"* with **19 tailored sales pages** and **20+ embedded forms, applications, and lead magnets** covering exactly the Novae-labeled items on Evert's board: Business Credit Builder, Business Funding, Business Debt Relief, Personal Loans, Debt Consolidation, Consumer Debt Relief, Instant Tax Refund, Student Loan & Auto Refi, Savings Accounts & Credit Cards ([novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/](https://novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/)).

### How Evert Is Using Novae

Mesa Group's own pages describe Novae as the infrastructure partner for their most impactful programs:

> "Novae powers some of Mesa's most impactful programs: business funding in all 50 states, debt relief for individuals and businesses, and a structured business credit-building program. When clients are ready to step into their financial potential, Novae is the infrastructure that makes it possible."
> — [mesagroupconsulting.com/our-partners](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/our-partners)

The affiliate disclosure adds: "Novae: Business funding and debt relief services (business and personal)" and "Novae and Partner Networks: Debt settlement and negotiation services" — Mesa receives a commission when clients secure funding or enroll in debt relief through Novae ([mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/affiliate-disclosure)).

This maps cleanly to the five Novae entries on Evert's Miro board:
- **Debt relief** → Novae Debt Help
- **Trust & Will plan** → Novae's Wills & Trusts (powered by Trust & Will)
- **Life insurance** → Novae Life Insurance (powered by PolicyGenius)
- **Business debt relief** → Novae Business Debt Help
- **Business credit** → Novae Business Credit Builder

Note on the life-insurance and estate-planning pages: Mesa Group's disclaimer separately names **PolicyGenius** and **Trust & Will** as their direct partners — that's accurate, because Novae itself runs those on PolicyGenius and Trust & Will infrastructure. So Evert can truthfully disclose either Novae (as the affiliate wrapper) or the underlying partner — both relationships exist. The "Novae" labels on his Miro board reflect that he's funneling those clicks through Novae's affiliate/co-brand stack to capture a commission, while still surfacing Trust & Will and PolicyGenius as the named partners in his FTC-compliant disclosures.

The Novae-driven pages live under:
- "For Consumers → Protection" (debt relief, Trust & Will planning, life insurance)
- "For Businesses → Business Services" (business funding, business credit builder, business debt relief, LLC formation)

---

## The Bigger Picture: Evert's Two-Pillar Funnel Strategy

The picture this paints is a deliberately built **two-pillar affiliate model** that lets Mesa Group monetize the same website traffic across two very different verticals:

| Customer need | Evert's "own" service | Affiliate partner that closes the lead |
|---|---|---|
| Fix credit | Credit repair (Mesa360 program, CROA-compliant) | SmartCredit (cross-sold as the monitoring tool) |
| Rebuild credit | Credit-building recommendations | Ava Finance, CreditStrong, Self, RentReporters, Rental Kharma, BoomPay, Experian Boost |
| Compare consumer loans/cards | (none — outbound) | **SuperMoney** (5 pages on his Miro board) |
| Solve personal debt | Debt-relief referral | **Novae** |
| Get life insurance | Quote comparison | **Novae → PolicyGenius** |
| Plan an estate | Wills/Trusts | **Novae → Trust & Will** |
| Fund or repair a business | Funding consulting + referrals | **Novae** (Business Credit, Business Funding, Business Debt Help, LLC Formation) |

A few contextual details that explain why he landed on these two specific partners:

1. **Coverage gaps.** A credit-repair client who is suddenly approved for new credit usually needs somewhere to *use* that credit. SuperMoney's pre-qualification engine is one of the easiest ways to monetize that traffic across personal loans, auto refi, student loan refi, debt consolidation, and cards — exactly the five pages Evert is building.

2. **Speed to launch.** Both programs emphasize that publishers can be live quickly. SuperMoney's Money Marketplace is an embeddable widget ([supermoney.com/monetize/money-marketplace](https://www.supermoney.com/monetize/money-marketplace)), and Novae's Co-Brand is explicitly marketed as a "turn-key web package… with zero lift" ([novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/](https://novaemoney.com/cobrand-program/)). For a small Bakersfield operation with a 5-person team, that's the cheapest way to add nine monetization pages without building lender integrations in-house.

3. **Recurring + residual revenue.** Mesa Group's own conflict-of-interest disclosure admits that subscription-style products create ongoing commission income. Novae's model leans heavily on residual commissions and rank-based bonuses; SuperMoney pays per qualified lead. Together they produce a mix of one-time payouts (loan originations), recurring payouts (subscriptions, debt-program retainers), and team-based overrides (Novae rank advancement).

4. **Geographic / demographic focus.** Both Novae and Mesa Group openly target underserved communities and bilingual (English/Spanish) consumers — Mesa explicitly markets "trilingual service" (English, Spanish, Punjabi) from Bakersfield ([mesagroupconsulting.com/author/evert-calderon](https://www.mesagroupconsulting.com/author/evert-calderon)), and Novae's stated mission is "financial inclusion" for underserved markets ([novaemoney.com/](https://novaemoney.com/)).

5. **FTC compliance.** Mesa Group has clearly invested in compliance — the affiliate disclosure walks through every required element under 16 CFR Part 255, the disclaimer explains CROA rights in plain English, and SuperMoney/Novae are both named partners on the published pages. That level of disclosure is unusual for a small affiliate site and suggests Evert is operating this as a real business, not a side hustle.

---

## Risks and Caveats Worth Knowing

**Novae's reputation is materially riskier than SuperMoney's.** [behindmlm.com](https://behindmlm.com/mlm-reviews/novae-money-review-financial-services-rebrand-stock-fraud/) flags several issues:
- Unregistered share offers ("company stock" for top rank) that are likely illegal under SEC rules.
- Founder Reco McDaniel's prior association with the collapsed WakeUpNow scheme.
- Compensation plan that is recruitment-incentivized (recruiting begins at rank two).
- Description as "largely a commission aggregator, not a provider" — most services are third-party referrals ([jessesingh.org review](https://jessesingh.org/novae-money-review/)).

The BBB's Direct Selling Self-Regulatory Council opened **monitoring case #231-2025** over income claims made by Novae's salesforce ([bbbprograms.org](https://bbbprograms.org/programs/advertising/dssrc/cases/novae)). Consumer reviews are mixed (ComplaintsBoard shows a 3.9-star average with complaints about service responsiveness and refunds) ([complaintsboard.com/novae-b144702](https://www.complaintsboard.com/novae-b144702)). None of this means Mesa's arrangement is improper, but it's a materially different risk profile from SuperMoney's (a mainstream comparison site with institutional certifications).

**What I couldn't confirm:**
- **Exact commission rates and EPCs** — Mesa says specific amounts are confidential under NDA with partners, and Novae doesn't publish rates in detail.
- **Which Novae tier Evert is enrolled at** (Basic, Pro, Co-Brand, or white-label). The fact that the new pages will live *on mesagroupconsulting.com* strongly suggests a Co-Brand or direct-affiliate setup (not a separate replicated NovaeMoney.com site), but the precise tier is private.
- **Whether team-building/recruitment is active** — Novae's compensation plan provides for override commissions across ten generations of recruited affiliates, so Evert could in principle be earning from recruited affiliates beneath him, not just from customer product sales. This is not confirmed.
- **Whether any referral revenue actually flows** — the pages are described as "new" on Evert's Miro board, so there is no public performance data.
- **Whether Novae's loan pages are themselves powered by SuperMoney** — the structural similarity exists, but no public source confirms an interconnection.
- **Regulatory exposure beyond CROA** — state debt-settlement licensing for Novae's debt-help referrals routed through Mesa, telemarketing/FCC rules on lead forms, and the FTC's recent crackdown on affiliate-driven credit-repair funnels are not addressed in Mesa's published materials.

**Income-disclosure note:** The "$1,408 average participant earnings in 2023" figure is Novae's own DSA-required disclosure, but it includes affiliates at every tier, full-time and part-time. It should not be read as a typical or expected income for someone like Evert who is using Novae as a supplementary monetization layer rather than as a primary MLM-style income stream.

Per the FY2024 10-K (filed March 20, 2025), vTv Therapeutics' total share-based compensation (SBC) expense rose from approximately **$1.578 million in FY2023 to $2.757 million in FY2024**, an absolute increase of **$1.179 million (+74.7%)**, broken down as follows (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000014/vtvt-20241231.htm; https://app.edgar.tools/companies/VTVT/disclosures/stock-compensation):

|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | $0.425M | $1.153M | **$1.578M** |
| 2024 | $0.742M | $2.015M | **$2.757M** |
| Change | +$0.317M (+74.6%) | +$0.862M (+74.8%) | **+$1.179M (+74.7%)** |

The G&A component accounted for roughly 73% of the total SBC dollar increase. The FY2024 10-K MD&A specifically attributes approximately **$0.8 million** of the overall $1.7 million G&A expense increase to higher share-based compensation, alongside $1.0 million in higher payroll costs (https://ebs.publicnow.com/view/8E872306EC63F9ED958BEA33200ECEDF1DA6312D). The company recognizes no tax benefit on these awards because it maintains a full valuation allowance against deferred tax assets, so every SBC dollar flows directly to net loss.

The 2024 jump was largely driven by new stock option awards issued in connection with vTv's **February 27, 2024 private placement**, which vest ratably over three years (rather than four years for standard grants) and have a 10-year contractual life.

## 2. Stock-Based Compensation Increase: Q3 2024 to Q3 2025 (R&D and G&A)

Using both the **three-month Q3** and the **nine-month YTD** data from the Q3 2025 10-Q (filed November 6, 2025; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000060/vtvt-20250930.htm) and Q3 2024 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148924000075/vtvt-20240930.htm):

### Three Months Ended September 30

| Line Item | Q3 2024 ($000) | Q3 2025 ($000) | Change | % Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Research and development | 228 | 311 | +$83K | +36.4% |
| General and administrative | 625 | 696 | +$71K | +11.4% |
| **Total SBC** | **853** | **1,007** | **+$154K** | **+18.1%** |

### Nine Months Ended September 30

| Line Item | 9M 2024 ($000) | 9M 2025 ($000) | Change | % Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Research and development | 511 | 845 | +$334K | +65.4% |
| General and administrative | 1,421 | 1,905 | +$484K | +34.1% |
| **Total SBC** | **1,932** | **2,750** | **+$818K** | **+42.3%** |

The R&D component rose fastest in percentage terms, consistent with the Q3 2025 earnings release noting that R&D expense growth reflected "increases in payroll and share-based expenses" tied to the ramp of the cadisegliatin Phase 3 CATT1 program (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000058/vtvt-20250930xexx991pressr.htm). The escalation continued: total annual SBC reached **$3.775 million in FY2025** (R&D $1.124M + G&A $2.651M), representing a **+36.9%** increase over FY2024 and a **+139.2%** cumulative increase over FY2023.

## 3. Stock Options at $11.81 and Talent Retention Strategy

In connection with the February 27, 2024 private placement, CEO Paul Sekhri received **89,212 stock options at an exercise price of $11.81**—precisely matching the PIPE price paid by institutional investors (Samsara BioCapital, JDRF T1D Fund, and others). The grant carried **accelerated three-year vesting** (rather than the standard four years for employee plan options) and a 10-year contractual term (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000119312524049260/d754681d8k.htm; https://app.edgar.tools/companies/VTVT/disclosures/stock-compensation).

Several aspects of this grant reveal the talent-retention approach:

- **Alignment with institutional pricing:** Setting the exercise price equal to the institutional PIPE price framed the award as "fair value" at grant while creating asymmetric upside for the executive as the stock moves.
- **Accelerated vesting schedule:** Three-year (rather than four-year) vesting provided faster access to gains—a stronger near-term retention tool during the pivotal Phase 3 ramp.
- **Comprehensive retention push:** Sekhri's base salary was simultaneously raised from $480,000 to $650,000 (+35.4%), paired with a one-time $471,042 cash bonus, signaling that vTv deployed multiple levers (cash and equity) to retain leadership.
- **Heavy ongoing equity reliance:** In Q1 2025, an additional 320,816 options were granted at a weighted-average exercise price of $19.66, bringing total outstanding options to 981,844 by March 31, 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000026/vtvt-20250331.htm).

The wider option-pool roll-forward for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 is even more revealing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000060/vtvt-20250930.htm):

| Event | Number of Shares | Weighted-Avg. Exercise Price |
|---|---|---|
| Outstanding at December 31, 2024 | 705,593 | **$35.85** |
| **Granted** | **388,816** | **$19.67** |
| Exercised | (20,719) | $11.81 |
| Forfeited/Expired | (66,384) | $112.16 |
| Outstanding at September 30, 2025 | 1,007,306 | $25.07 |
| Exercisable at September 30, 2025 | 372,211 | $37.11 |

Several retention-strategy implications emerge:

1. The 9M 2025 grants were struck at **$19.67—roughly 55% of the $35.85** legacy weighted-average strike outstanding at year-end 2024 and far below the $112.16 weighted-average strike of awards that were forfeited or expired during 9M 2025. Management is replacing deeply out-of-the-money, retention-impotent legacy awards with newly attainable strikes.
2. The grant-date fair value rose to **$15.00 per option** in 9M 2025 (from $14.85 in 9M 2024) under Black-Scholes, with the lower strikes increasing both intrinsic and time-value components.
3. With the share price well below the $35.85 legacy weighted-average (and dramatically below $112.16), prior-cycle retention options had become economically inert. The decision to grant new options at $19.67 effectively **resets the in-the-money hurdle closer to current trading levels**, restoring retention value for key personnel—particularly important given the CFO transition in May 2025 (Dr. Michael Tung appointed) and CEO Sekhri driving the Phase 3 launch.
4. The unrecognized stock-based compensation pool stands at approximately **$6.2 million**, expected to be amortized over a weighted-average of 2.6 years, extending the equity-based retention lock-in horizon through 2027–2028 (https://ir.vtvtherapeutics.com/static-files/2123593c-d51e-4c21-9cb5-4d84bdd79c80).

In effect, vTv is paying for talent retention with freshly issued equity at progressively lower strikes—a strategy that signals (a) limited cash for retention bonuses and (b) management's willingness to lean on the equity ledger to keep the team intact through the Phase 3 readout.

## 4. Warrant Overhang and Future Dilution Risks

vTv's equity overhang operates through three layered channels on top of the option pool:

### (a) February 27, 2024 Private Placement Pre-Funded Warrants

vTv sold 464,377 Class A shares at $11.81/share plus pre-funded warrants for 3,853,997 shares at an $11.80 strike ($0.01 exercise price), raising approximately **$51.0 million gross**. A subsequent March 5, 2024 letter agreement exchanged 116,493 of those shares for 116,590 additional pre-funded warrants (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000053/vtvt-20250630.htm). These pre-funded warrants are exercisable at any time, have **no expiration**, and carry only a $0.01 strike—they are **economically equivalent to already-issued shares** and represent the largest single source of potential dilution.

### (b) August 2025 Private Placement Warrants

The Q3 2025 Statement of Stockholders' Equity records an August 2025 issuance of 682,018 shares (at $15.265) together with equity-classified warrants, with net proceeds of approximately **$77.5 million** (https://ir.vtvtherapeutics.com/static-files/2123593c-d51e-4c21-9cb5-4d84bdd79c80; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000119312525193486/d52598d8k.htm). The structure included:

- **4,561,714 pre-funded warrants** at a $15.255 strike ($0.01 exercise price)
- **5,243,732 Common Warrants** at a **$22.71 exercise price**, expiring on the earlier of 5 years or **90 days after positive CATT1 data announcement**

The 2025 PIPE therefore created potential additional proceeds of up to **$119 million** from Common Warrant exercises if the stock price exceeds $22.71—and offered a built-in **paradox**: positive CATT1 Phase 3 clinical data would trigger a 90-day exercise window that could flood the market with new shares precisely when good news is being announced.

### (c) Legacy Warrants

Letter-agreement warrants (~70,639 shares at various strikes) and CinRx warrants (30,000 shares at ~$28.80, conditional on FDA approval or acquisition) remain outstanding at immaterial intrinsic values; warrant liabilities stood at $37K (related-party) and $57K (non-related-party) per the Q3 2025 press release tables.

### Combined Overhang

| Source | Approximate Shares |
|---|---|
| Class A common shares outstanding (Nov 6, 2025) | 3,938,018 |
| February 2024 pre-funded warrants ($0.01 strike, no expiration) | ~3,853,997 |
| August 2025 pre-funded warrants ($0.01 strike) | ~4,561,714 |
| Stock options outstanding (Sep 30, 2025) | 1,007,306 |
| Common stock warrants ($22.71 strike) | 5,243,732 |
| Class B common stock (controlled by M&F TTP Holdings / MacAndrews & Forbes) | 241 |
| **Fully diluted share count** | **~18.6 million** |

### Share-Count Expansion Already Realized

Class A common shares outstanding grew from **2,612,257 at December 31, 2024 to 3,938,018 at November 6, 2025**, an increase of **1,325,761 shares (≈ +50.8%) in less than a year** (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1641489/000164148925000060/vtvt-20250930.htm). Weighted-average diluted shares used in EPS rose from **5,456,307 (Q3 2024) to 8,055,940 (Q3 2025)**—a **≈ +47.6%** expansion quarter-over-quarter. Over a two-year horizon, weighted-average Class A shares outstanding rose from 2,084,973 in 2023 to 5,771,052 in 2024 to 8,423,632 in 2025—a **+304% increase** in two years.

## 5. Implications for Existing Shareholders

- **Per-share value erosion is real and accelerating.** A hypothetical holder with 1% of Class A stock at year-end 2023 (~20,850 shares) would have seen proportional ownership decline to approximately **0.24%** of the fully diluted share count by year-end 2025—a ~76% reduction in economic interest without selling a single share.
- **EPS optics have worsened.** Net loss attributable to vTv shareholders widened from $4.78M (Q3 2024) to $8.70M (Q3 2025); per-share, the loss moved from $(0.88) to $(1.08)—share-count growth worsened per-share optics despite the absolute loss being driven primarily by milestone accruals and R&D ramp (https://ir.vtvtherapeutics.com/node/10966/pdf).
- **The unrecognized SBC pool of ~$6.2M** will continue to be amortized over roughly 2.6 years, meaning GAAP losses will continue to bear a non-cash but real dilution component through at least 2027–2028.
- **The 2024 Equity Incentive Plan** authorized 750,000 shares initially with an **automatic annual 4% increase** provision (based on total shares plus pre-funded warrants), ensuring the equity-compensation pool grows perpetually alongside the expanding share count—an embedded, self-reinforcing dilution mechanism.
- **No anti-dilution mechanisms are in evidence.** There are no buybacks, no anti-dilution clauses, and no non-dilutive financing paths visible. The 10-Q notes the Company "continues to evaluate" alternatives including ATM usage (TD Cowen facility), potential debt financing, or preferred equity—each adding further dilution risk.
- **Controlling-shareholder dynamics:** M&F TTP Holdings (MacAndrews & Forbes) controls the Class B interest and the Company's letter-agreement warrants. While this reduces the likelihood of a near-term block sale, it represents a permanent claim on future equity value held by a related party.

## 6. Equity Financing Strategy: Overall Assessment

vTv's equity financing strategy is **structurally dilutive and is being layered across three reinforcing channels**:

1. **Compensation layer—pay executives and key employees in options because cash is constrained.** The 2025 cash position of ~$98.5M (September 30, 2025) versus a 9M operating cash loss of roughly $22M leaves limited room for non-equity compensation. The lower-strike, more frequent option grants (388,816 at $19.67 in 9M 2025, replacing $112.16-strike forfeitures) are essentially cash-substitute retention tools (https://ir.vtvtherapeutics.com/node/10966/pdf).

2. **Capital-raising layer—fund Phase 3 cadisegliatin development through pre-funded warrants and private placements rather than debt or non-dilutive sources.** Two raises within 18 months—$51M (Feb 2024) + ~$77.5M net (Aug 2025)—total approximately $128.5M, both structured around $0.01-strike pre-funded warrants that are economically equivalent to common stock and already counted in basic EPS.

3. **Related-party overhang layer—Class B interests and letter-agreement warrants held by the controlling shareholder represent permanent claims on future equity value** that do not require near-term disposition but cap the long-run economic interest available to common holders.

### Conclusion

Until cadisegliatin produces a value-creating event (Phase 3 CATT1 readout expected 2H 2026), the equity float will likely continue to expand, with the $0.01-strike pre-funded warrants virtually guaranteeing that share count will rise regardless of market conditions. Existing shareholders are funding both Phase 3 clinical execution and management retention via two parallel equity channels—option grants and pre-funded warrant private placements—with no offsetting buybacks, anti-dilution mechanisms, or non-dilutive financing alternatives visible.

Three near-term risk vectors warrant monitoring:
- **Pace of unrecognized SBC amortization** through 2027–2028
- **Equity Incentive Plan's automatic 4% annual increase**, which continually replenishes the dilution pipeline
- **Future PIPE or ATM utilization** that would layer additional dilution onto the existing 5.3M+ Common Warrant and ~8.4M pre-funded warrant overhang

The most acute strategic risk is counterintuitive: a **positive Phase 3 CATT1 readout could paradoxically trigger the most severe near-term dilution event** via the 90-day Common Warrant exercise window in the August 2025 PIPE, converting the company's best possible clinical outcome into an immediate flood of new shares.

## 7. Key Sources

# NCD Public Issue Review — India
## Cut-off: 8 December 2025 | Retiree Fixed-Income Mandate | Institutional Research Standard

## 1. Executive Summary

As of 8-Dec-2025, **three secured NCD public issues** are actively open for retail subscription on BSE, with effective yields spanning **10.10% p.a. to 13.80% p.a.** — a 370 bps spread that materially diverges in expected loss content. A fourth (KLM Axiva Finvest, open 1–12 Dec) closes before the week-end, and a near-sovereign **REC Limited AAA private placement** opens 9-Dec-2025 as the relevant benchmark anchor. For a retiree, no NCD-specific senior-citizen coupon premium exists on any of the issues in scope; the senior-citizen advantage lies entirely in tax treatment (basic exemption / Section 87A rebate under the New Tax Regime up to ₹12L income, or the OLD regime's ₹3,00,000 basic exemption).

**Headline flags:**
- **Edelweiss Financial Services (EFSL)** — CRISIL A+/Stable; consolidated D/E 3.02–3.43x depending on reporting date; net debt down ~17–27% YoY; ECLF/eARC RBI supervisory episode (May-24) lifted Dec-24. Investment-grade; suitable for moderate allocation.

## 5. Post-Tax Yield Analysis

### 5.1 Tax Framework (FY 2025-26 / AY 2026-27)
- **TDS under Sec 193:** 10% on listed NCD interest (post Finance Act 2023 amendment, which withdrew the demat-listed exemption from FY24).
- **Interest income classification:** "Income from Other Sources"; taxed at the individual's marginal slab rate.
- **Capital gains:** Sale before 12 months → at slab rate; after 12 months (listed) → 10% LTCG without indexation; unlisted long-term (36 months) → 20% with indexation.
- **Sec 80TTB's ₹50,000 interest exemption applies only to bank and post-office deposits — NOT corporate NCDs.** This is a common retiree misconception.
- **No NCD-specific senior-citizen coupon premium** exists on any of the issues in scope. None of the December 2025 NCD public issues provide senior-citizen coupons. The corporate FD +0.35–0.50% senior-citizen premium is issuer-specific and not observed here.
- **Form 15H** can suppress TDS if total income is below taxable limit.

Sources: [RRFinance — Taxation on Bonds & NCDs in India](https://www.rrfinance.com/Blogs/taxation-on-bonds-and-ncds.aspx); [ICMAI Article on Sec 193 amendment](https://icmai.in/TaxationPortal/upload/DT/Article/123_0911_23.pdf); [EZBond TDS Rules](https://ezbond.in/learn/taxation/tds-on-ncd-interest); [PrimeInvestor Jan-24](https://primeinvestor.in/reports/how-are-g-secs-bonds-and-ncds-taxed/); [GoldenPi FAQ](https://goldenpi.com/faq/collection-details/are-ncd-taxable); [EZBond Calculator](https://ezbond.in/calculators/ncd-returns).

### 5.2 Senior Citizen vs. Generic Investor — Quantitative Post-Tax Yields

| Investor Profile | Marginal Rate (incl. 4% cess) | REC Post-Tax (8.55%) | EFSL Post-Tax (10.10%) | MML Post-Tax (11.73%) | PCL Post-Tax (13.80%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **30% bracket** (Old/New Regime) | 31.2% | 5.89% | **6.95%** | **8.07%** | **9.49%** |
| 20% bracket (New Regime) | 20.8% | 6.77% | 8.00% | 9.29% | 10.93% |
| 5% bracket (New Regime) | 10.4% | 7.66% | 9.05% | 10.51% | 12.36% |
| Senior citizen — NIL slab (income ≤ ₹12L, New Regime, Sec 87A rebate) | 0.0% | **8.55%** | **10.10%** | **11.73%** | **13.80%** |
| Senior citizen — only-NCD income ₹5L (Old Sr. Reg.) | ~2.08% effective | 8.37% | 9.89% | 11.49% | 13.51% |

**Method:** Post-Tax Yield = Pre-Tax Effective Yield × (1 – Marginal Tax Rate incl. 4% H&E Cess).

### 5.3 Senior Citizen Differential — Conclusion
- Under the NEW regime (default from FY24), senior citizens receive **no marginal slab advantage** vs. other individuals.
- Under the OLD regime, the ₹50,000 higher basic exemption (₹3L vs ₹2.5L) translates to only ~₹10,400 in incremental annual tax savings for a retiree in the 5% bracket — i.e., ~0.10% net yield differential, **immaterial relative to coupon spread**.
- **Budget 2025 ₹12L Section 87A rebate** under the NEW regime effectively eliminates tax for retirees with total income (including NCD interest) ≤ ₹12L (~₹12.75L with standard deduction). **However, NCD interest counts toward taxable income, unlike tax-free bond interest** — retirees must monitor this threshold to preserve the rebate. Source: [The Hindu BusinessLine Mar-25](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/portfolio/personal-finance/how-tax-free-bonds-aid-senior-citizens-and-retirees/article69278717.ece).
- **For retiree: ranking of post-tax carry is preserved as EFSL < MML < PCL regardless of senior-citizen status.** The senior-citizen edge is most relevant where NCD interest is the dominant income source and the retiree files Form 15H to suppress TDS.

## 7. Historical Precedents & Pattern Recognition

### 7.1 Indian NCD Default Cycle (IL&FS → DHFL Era)
- **IL&FS (Sep-2018):** AAA-rated infra lender defaulted on Rs.90,000+ Cr of group debt, triggered NBFC funding crisis and government-supervised board takeover. Secured NCD holders received partial recoveries over 5+ years.
- **DHFL (Jun-2019):** Went from AAA → D in 12 months. Recovery on secured NCDs: **<Rs.2 lakh series → 100% principal; Rs.2–10 lakh series → 43.82% cash; >Rs.10 lakh → cash + Piramal debentures; FD holders → ~23%**.
- **Reliance Home Finance (2019):** AA+ → D in 9 months; unsecured subordinated NCDs were the first to absorb losses.
- **Lesson:** Public, secured NCDs are not retail-safe by construction; recovery depends entirely on issuer balance sheet and collateral cover.

Sources: [Catalyst Trusteeship RHFL Status Report](https://catalysttrustee.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Reliance-Home-Finance-Limited_Status-Report_08.08.2023.pdf); [BondLab India — When Indian Bonds Went Wrong](https://bondlab.in/guides/bond-defaults-india-history/); [Indian Express — DHFL retail money](https://indianexpress.com/article/business/companies/rs-15000-crore-of-retail-investor-money-stuck-in-dhfl-6136906/).

### 7.2 Recent NCD Subscription Patterns
- **Indel Money (Oct-25)** — BBB+/Stable, yield up to 13.44%: **oversubscribed 3.15x** (Rs.472.79 Cr bids).
- **Adani Enterprises (Jul-25)** — CARE A+/Positive, yield up to 9.30%: **oversubscribed 3x on day 1**.
- **Nido Home Finance (Jan-25)** — oversubscribed 2.05x.
- **Edelweiss Financial Services (current)** — **3.30x overall (4.57x retail)**.
- **Muthoot Mercantile (current)** — **2.35x** (institutional: 0.00x).
- **Prachay Capital (current)** — **1.73x** (9.86x retail — strong retail HNI tilt).
- **KLM Axiva Finvest** — institutional participation negligible.

**Pattern:** high-yield (12%+) NBFC paper consistently attracts 1.5–3x oversubscription from retail; investment-grade issues fill within 2–4 days at the top of the rate cycle. **Institutional non-participation (0.00x on MML; near-zero on PCL retail pattern) is a meaningful credit-quality signal** — institutional desks underwrite credit far more conservatively than retail HNI.

Sources: [The Hindu BusinessLine — Indel Money](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/indel-moneys-ncd-issue-oversubscribed-by-315/article70239583.ece); [Economic Times — Adani Enterprises 3x oversubscribed](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/bonds/adani-enterprises-rs-500-crore-ncd-issue-oversubscribed-3x/articleshow/122352660.cms); [Chittorgarh live subscription trackers](https://www.chittorgarh.com/ncd_subscription/edelweiss-financial-services-ncd-december-2025/367/).

### 7.3 Cycle Positioning
The current 2023–2025 cycle has seen a proliferation of BBB-rated NBFC NCDs offering 10–14% yields — **reminiscent of the 2018–2019 cycle when IL&FS and DHFL collapses exposed the risks of lower-rated NCDs**. The sharp repricing of BBB vs. AAA spreads (currently 275–525 bps) reflects yield hunger but also embedded credit risk. KLM Axiva's trajectory (initial BBB/Stable → deterioration within 12 months → downgrade to BBB-/Negative) mirrors patterns seen with multiple microfinance-oriented NBFCs in 2019–2020.

---

## 8. Competitive Positioning & Relative Value

### 8.1 Yield Anchor Comparison (8-Dec-2025)
- **India 10-yr G-Sec yield:** ~6.46% (post 5-Dec-25 RBI cut) — risk-free benchmark. Source: [RBI Press Release 5-Dec-25](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=61749).
- **RBI Repo Rate:** 5.25% (cut 25 bps on 5-Dec-25 from 5.50%); SDF 5.00%; MSF/Bank Rate 5.50%.
- **5-yr PSU bank FD rate:** ~6.50–7.25% (SBI 6.50%, top private banks up to 7.25% for senior citizens).
- **RBI Floating Rate Savings Bonds:** 8.05% (currently) for retail — government-backed.
- **Tax-free PSU bonds (historical):** 5.0–5.5% pre-tax = ~7.5–8.0% post-tax equivalent.

### 8.2 Spread vs. G-Sec (10-yr ~6.46%)

| Issuer | Eff. Yield | Spread vs. 10-yr G-Sec | Spread vs. REC AAA | Risk-Adjusted View |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REC Limited (AAA) | 8.55% | +209 bps | — | Sovereign-grade reference |
| **EDSL (A+)** | **10.10%** | **+364 bps** | **+155 bps** | **Best risk-adjusted carry; ~15–20 bps/notch is fair** |
| KLM Axiva (BBB) | 11.30% | +484 bps | +275 bps | High premium for sub-investment-grade boundary |
| MML (BBB) | 11.73% | +527 bps | +318 bps | Gold-loan NBFC sector premium |
| PCL (BBB-) | 13.80% | +734 bps | +525 bps | Speculative premium; concentration risk under-priced |

### 8.3 Relative Value Ranking
- **REC Limited** = benchmark anchor (private placement only).
- **EFSL** offers the best **credit-quality-per-bp**: ~360 bps spread for A+ NBFC parent with credible net-leverage repair.
- **MML** offers sector best-practice risk-adjusted carry (CRAR 25%+, asset-side gold cover) at sector-norm D/E.
- **PCL** offers the highest carry but also carries the **highest idiosyncratic risk** — sub-investment grade territory, geographic concentration, recently converted to public limited (Oct-24), 87% NCD funding concentration flagged by CRISIL ([CRISIL PCL Aug-25](https://www.crisilratings.com/mnt/winshare/Ratings/RatingList/RatingDocs/PrachayCapitalLimited_August%2012_%202025_RR_374243.html)).
- **KLM Axiva** — pattern-recognition case suggests BBB microfinance/gold-MFI NBFC paper is the riskiest bucket in this rate cycle.

---

## 9. Comprehensive Risk Assessment

### 9.1 Issuer-Specific Tail Risks
- **EFSL:** (i) ECLF/eARC RBI supervisory history (May-24 → lifted 17-Dec-24); (ii) gross leverage 3.43x in a rate-cut cycle puts NIM compression pressure on subsidiaries; (iii) NCD funding model has been EFSL's major incremental funding source — over-reliance is structural; (iv) ISCR of 1.05x is thin; (v) gross Stage-3 assets in the group ran at Rs.13,155 Cr as of FY23 (held in EARC); (vi) group-level rating contagion risk.
- **MML:** (i) IND BBB — at the lower band of investment grade; (ii) gold-loan business is concentrated and cyclical (gold price drawdown can compress LTVs); (iii) FY25 gross NPA spiked to 1.60% (Sep-25), implying asset-quality volatility; (iv) leverage of 4.69x gross means a 200-bp rate shock + 5% NPA spike could threaten capital; (v) relatively short operating history under the "Mercantile" branding; (vi) high D/E flagged by issuer itself as risk factor #9.
- **PCL:** (i) BBB- is one notch above the BB speculative cutoff — single-notch downgrade would re-rate paper sharply; (ii) **asset concentration** in real-estate developers; (iii) **geographic concentration** in Pune/Maharashtra; (iv) **customer concentration** risk flagged by Infomerics explicitly; (v) concentrated funding base (87% NCD reliance per CRISIL); (vi) only 2nd public NCD issue (Feb-25 was the first); (vii) AUM growth dependent on continued real-estate cycle buoyancy; (viii) absolute net worth small relative to issue size.
- **KLM Axiva:** (i) Subsequent Aug-2026 deterioration (D/E to 7.75x, PAT -56%, downgrade to BBB-/Negative) confirms BBB microfinance/MFI NBFC risk pattern; (ii) institutional non-participation in primary book; (iii) gross NPA spike to 3.17%.

### 9.2 Systemic / Macro Tail Risks
- **Rate-cut transmission risk:** RBI cut to 5.25% on 5-Dec-25 with neutral stance — possible further cuts to terminal 5.00% would compress reinvestment yields on these NCDs at maturity (reinvestment risk for retiree living off coupons).
- **Credit-cycle reversal:** Current FY25 default rate of 0.5% is near cyclical lows; mean-reversion risk as rate cycle bottoms.
- **NBFC funding stress:** History (IL&FS, DHFL) shows NBFCs are first hit in liquidity crunches.
- **Listing liquidity:** All three retail-accessible issues are BSE-only listed; secondary-market exit is constrained; secondary spread could widen during a credit shock, trapping investors who need liquidity.

### 9.3 Regulatory & Structural Risks
- **SEBI NCS Regulations 2021:** Mandates debenture trustee, in-principle listing approval, dematerialized form, default disclosure. Issuer cannot be in default >6 months to issue new NCDs. Provides framework but does not eliminate loss risk. Source: [SEBI NCS Regulations 2021](https://aibi.org.in/SEBI_Regulations/SEBI(Issue_and_Listing_of_Non_Convertible_Securities)Regulations_2021[Last_amended_on_September_18_2024].pdf); [TaxGuru — SEBI NCS Regulations summary](https://taxguru.in/sebi/salient-features-sebi-ncs-regulations-2021.html).
- **RBI classification:** Prachay Capital is "Base Layer" NBFC; Muthoot Mercantile and KLM Axiva are "Middle Layer"; Edelweiss is a systemically important NBFC (NBFC-ICC). These classifications affect capital requirements and supervisory intensity.
- **SEBI tightening of disclosure norms:** The deliberate delay in uploading Muthoot Mercantile's offer document was flagged by reviewers as a compliance concern. Source: [Chittorgarh MML review](https://www.chittorgarh.com/ncd_review/muthoot-mercantile-ncd-december-2025/4878/).
- **TDS default risk:** Form 15G/15H filing at application is critical — failure results in cash-flow drag of 10% on day-one coupon.

---

## 10. Regulatory & Policy Landscape

- **RBI MPC 5-Dec-2025:** Repo rate cut to **5.25%** (25 bps cut), neutral stance. SDF at 5.00%, MSF/Bank Rate at 5.50%. GDP growth forecast upgraded to 7.3% (from 6.8%); inflation forecast 2% (from 2.6%). Announced Rs.1 lakh Cr OMO purchases and $5 bn USD/INR sell-buy swap in Dec-25 — liquidity supportive of bond markets. Sources: [RBI Press Release 5-Dec-25](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=61749); [RBI MPC Minutes Dec-25](https://api.policyindex.ai/demo/PR1739MPCMinutesDec2025FINAL.pdf); [Economic Times MPC Dec-25](https://m.economictimes.com/news/economy/policy/mpc-meeting-today-highlights-repo-rate-decision-key-updates-monetary-policy-committee-news/amp_articleshow/125780144.cms).
- **Implication for new NCDs:** Rate-cut cycle generally compresses yield expectations, but the cycle has already lowered rates; the high-coupon NCDs (MML, PCL) compensate investors for credit risk, not rate risk. Long-tenor (120-mo EFSL, 60-mo PCL) crystallizes rate-cut risk at maturity.
- **Tax regime:** Finance Act 2023 amendment (Sec 193) continues to apply TDS on listed NCD interest — confirmed for FY 2025-26. Budget 2025 increased Section 87A rebate to ₹12L under the New Tax Regime, eliminating tax for retirees with total income ≤ ₹12L (~₹12.75L with standard deduction).

---

## 11. Forward Curve & Leading Indicators

- **Indicative secondary-market G-Sec curve:** 1Y ~5.9%, 5Y ~6.4%, 10Y ~6.46%, 40Y ~7.10%.
- **Implied forward path:** Consensus expects 25 bps more cuts to a terminal 5.00% repo, implying corporate-bond yields drift 20–40 bps lower over 12 months. This implies **reinvestment risk for retiree living off NCD coupons at maturity**.
- **Leading indicator for credit:** India Ratings D-U ratio at 0.28 (improving) and multi-notch downgrades at 0.5% (declining). Watch the FY26 H2 cycle.
- **Retail credit demand:** India Ratings flagged continued robust domestic consumption, benign commodity prices, and government infra spending — supportive of NBFC credit profiles for now. However, near-cycle-low default rates embed mean-reversion risk.
- **Institutional subscription trend:** Near-zero institutional participation in PCL, MML, and KLM Axiva primary books — a meaningful divergence from retail oversubscription; institutional credit underwriting is the more conservative signal.

---

## 12. Investment Thesis & Recommendation

### 12.1 Recommended Allocation Framework for Retiree

| Bucket | Issuer | Suggested Weight | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core fixed income | Government / RBI FRSB / SBI FD | 50–60% | Sovereign-grade; tax-efficient on Form 15H; reinvestment flexibility |
| Investment-grade NBFC carry | EFSL NCD (Series IX/X, 60–120 mo) | 15–25% | A+/Stable; modest spread over G-Sec; moderate credit risk |
| Yield-enhancement (small) | MML NCD (60/75 mo) | 5–15% | Gold-loan cover; CRAR cushion; acceptable at small weight |
| Tactical / opportunistic | PCL NCD (60 mo) | 0–5% | Speculative grade; concentrated risk; only for risk-tolerant |
| (If accessible) REC Limited | AAA | Up to 100% substitute for govt | Near-sovereign; 8.55% pre-tax / 8.55% post-tax for nil-slab retirees |

### 12.2 Specific Series Recommendations
- **Most defensive:** EFSL Series 10 (120-month Annual, 10.10% coupon) — highest coupon in the A+ category; REC liquidity offer (7-yr AAA, 8.55%) if private-placement access available.
- **Best yield with asset cover:** MML Series 8 (60-month Monthly, 10.75% coupon, 11.30% effective yield) or Series 9 (75-month Cumulative, 11.73% effective).
- **Highest carry / highest risk:** PCL Series 3 (60-month Monthly, 13.00% coupon, 13.80% effective).
- **Avoid for institutional mandates:** KLM Axiva — subsequent downgrading, 56% PAT collapse, gearing at 7.75x, negligible institutional subscription make this unsuitable.

### 12.3 Implementation Notes
- File Form 15H at allotment for TDS relief (if applicable).
- Senior-citizen retirees should consider **monthly-paying series** for cash-flow matching with monthly expenses.
- Long-tenor (120-mo EFSL or 60-mo PCL) crystallizes rate-cut risk — if reinvestment at maturity is the goal, this is acceptable; if capital preservation is the goal, prefer shorter tenor (24–36 mo) on EFSL.
- Diversify across issuers rather than concentrate in PCL carry.
- Monitor Section 87A rebate threshold (₹12L / ₹12.75L with standard deduction) under the New Tax Regime — NCD interest counts toward total income and could breach the rebate if not managed.

### 12.4 Suitability Review

| Investor Profile | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Conservative retiree (60–70 yrs), capital preservation priority | EFSL only — 30–40% of fixed-income sleeve, balance in RBI FRSB / bank FDs |
| Moderate retiree willing to accept A-category NBFC risk | EFSL 50% + MML 30% + sovereigns 20% |
| Aggressive retiree seeking yield, larger corpus | EFSL 30% + MML 40% + PCL 20% + sovereigns 10% |
| HNI / family-trust seeking 13%+ carry | PCL is the only option in retail-accessible issues; cap at 5–10% of fixed-income sleeve |
| Institutional HNI with private-placement access | REC Limited AAA — substitute for sovereign allocation |

---

## 13. Key Uncertainties

1. **RBI terminal rate path** — if cuts continue below 5%, NCD coupons may need to be repriced downward at maturity, eroding total carry (reinvestment risk).
2. **Real-estate cycle inflection** — PCL's asset quality is highly correlated to developer cashflows; a slowdown in Indian real estate would translate directly to NPA risk.
3. **Group-level rating contagion** — Edelweiss group's interconnected entities mean any future regulatory action against a subsidiary could pressure EFSL standalone ratings.
4. **Gold price volatility** — Muthoot Mercantile's loan book is gold-backed, but extreme gold-price drawdown can change LTV dynamics and trigger auction-related credit losses.
5. **Secondary-market liquidity** — All three retail-accessible issues are BSE-only listings; secondary spread could widen during a credit shock, trapping investors who need liquidity.
6. **Tax-regime selection** — Retirees must compare OLD vs. NEW regime carefully. Sec 87A rebate under NEW is generous but eliminates Sec 80TTB benefit (which doesn't apply to NCDs anyway).
7. **NCD senior-citizen misperception** — Many retail brokers still incorrectly cite "senior citizen NCD advantage"; in fact, no such coupon premium is in scope. Tax advantage (Form 15H / rebate) is the only differential.
8. **Data-integrity caveat** — Several retrieved sources carry post-dated timestamps (Apr-26, Jan-26, Aug-26); these have been used as forward-looking context where flagged, not as point-in-time readings. The primary 8-Dec-2025 snapshot relies on BSE filings, rating rationales current at that date, and prospectus documents.
