# Cold-Weather Mining Equipment Selection for Mongolia (–40°C): Caterpillar vs. Komatsu vs. Volvo CE vs. Russian/CIS Alternatives

## Executive Recommendation

For a –40°C mining fleet in Mongolia, **Caterpillar and Komatsu form the only credible primary-purchase basis** because both have full-line dealer operations (Barloworld Mongolia and Transwest Mongolia respectively), deep UB parts warehouses, component-rebuild centers, and Mongolian-language training programs. Komatsu has the stronger in-country mining track record (28+ 930E-4SE trucks operating at Oyu Tolgoi since 2012 [https://en.eot.mn/open-pit-mine]) while Caterpillar has the deepest after-sales infrastructure (~600 employees, ~36,000 SKUs / ~2.76 million part units across four Mongolian branches [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/barloworldmongolia_partsavailability-reliability-operationalexcellence-activity-7455421923053740032-dal1]). **Volvo CE should not be primary fleet** because no verifiable mining-class CE dealer with a bonded parts warehouse has been confirmed in Mongolia; Volvo parts arrive 5–7 days by air-freight from Mumbai [https://partstrading.com/suppliers/volvo-parts-mongolia/]. **BelAZ** is the only Western/CIS competitor with a documented –50°C factory rating across its product line and >200 units already operating in Mongolia [https://minprom.gov.by/belazy-serii-7513-budut-rabotat-v-pustyne-gobi/]. A Cat+Komatsu primary mix supplemented by BelAZ for cost-driven auxiliary haulage (and UZTM-KARTEX for grid-powered rope shovels) is the strongest structure.

---

## 1. Engineering for –40°C Operation

### 1.1 Caterpillar

Caterpillar's baseline cold-start rating for large hydraulic mining equipment is **–18°C (0°F)** with a 52°C upper limit; sustained operation below –10°C requires the optional **Cold Weather Package**, which adds engine coolant heaters, engine oil heaters, hydraulic oil heaters, cab pre-heaters, fuel preheaters, fuel blenders, hydraulic oil cooler bypass valves, and external 400V/208V three-phase power (~50 kW) [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210601-35dac-75766; https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20240220-31ab5-16ec1]. With the cold-start block-heater option on the Cat 395, machine cold-start capability extends to **–32°C (–25°F)** [https://www.cat.com/en_US/products/new/equipment/excavators/large-excavators/126440.html]. The Cat 6020B hydraulic mining shovel was validated for **modular field assembly at –30°C (–22°F)** with the same 14-day assembly time achieved in temperate conditions, giving operational confidence for –40°C deployment when paired with the Cold Weather Package [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20160201-48357-52819].

The Cat 793/797F mining trucks spec antifreeze/coolant protection to **–50°C (–58°F)** with engine coolant and oil heaters for cold-weather starts, automatic engine thermal management, variable-speed fans for low-temperature operation, electric- or air-start options, fuel filter with water separator and fuel heater, heated mirrors, modular HVAC, and a 36,510 BTU/hr (10.7 kW) cab heater rated to ambient **–30°C as standard**, with auxiliary cold-weather cab heating or Deluxe Cold Weather Cab available for lower ambient thresholds [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20240909-c65b1-7536b; https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20221205-dfa81-b707a]. The Cat 785/789D similarly offers antifreeze to –50°C, 240V coolant/oil heaters, deluxe cold-weather cab, and cold-weather start/brake-oil recirculating options [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20240802-58b3d-16a58; https://www.eltrakbulgaria.com/uploads/Products/NewSeries/MiningTrucks/789D.pdf]. The Cat 824 Wheel Dozer carries antifreeze rated to **–50°C** when arctic-configured [https://www.fabickcat.com/new-equipment/824-wheel-dozer/].

### 1.2 Komatsu

Komatsu Mining Germany rates its hydraulic shovels for ambient down to **–50°C** with preheating for diesel engine, water, hydraulic oil, and lubrication systems. Below –25°C normal operation halts and external electrical preheating must be engaged; hydraulic oil must reach –20°C (viscosity ~1000 cSt) before the main drive engine starts, with crankshaft held at half-rated speed until viscosity drops to 100–10 cSt. Arctic-package components include cast/forged structural elements, special-steel bolted connections, special-insulation cables, and ICE-Champion flexible high-pressure hoses with special-steel connectors [https://onemine.org/documents/adaptation-of-hydraulic-shovels-for-arctic-temperature-of-yakutia-region].

The Komatsu 930E-5, 980E-5, and 860E-1K support cold-weather packages with electric coolant/oil/hydraulic heaters, double-wall exhaust tubes, radiator shutters, cold-weather suspensions, and (on the 980E-5) **heated exhaust routing through the dump body** to prevent payload freeze-sticking — engineered for Canadian oil sands and directly applicable to Mongolian winter operations [https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/products/equipment/trucks/electric-drive-mining-trucks/980e-5; https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/products/equipment/trucks/electric-drive-mining-trucks/860e-1k; https://www.komatsu.jp/en/-/media/home/aboutus/innovation/technology/techreport/2017/en/180330_06e.pdf]. The 930E-5SE offers optional heated body, hot-start engine oil (220V), hot-start hydraulic oil, hot-start engine coolant (220V), and cold-weather suspensions [https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/products/equipment/trucks/electric-drive-mining-trucks/930e-5se].

Empirical Komatsu reliability: a Russian study of Komatsu D-375A/A5 dozers showed failure flow on basic components rising **2–6×** at low temperatures versus warm-season operations, with –25°C identified as the critical threshold for rubber/polymer embrittlement [https://exa.ai/library/publication/9vvm1yl0lv4]. Komatsu also offers a **Komatsu PC400-7 (JPN) Extreme Cold Terrain Spec** excavator variant with a factory winterization assembly manual [https://manuals-komatsu.com/shop/komatsu-pdf-download-1/pc400-7jpn-extreme-cold-terrain-spec-s-n-50001-up-field-assembly-manual-english/]. Boliden's Arctic mines in Sweden/Finland operate Komatsu 930E trucks and L2350 wheel loaders at **–40°C** under Cummins cost-per-hour service agreements with PrevenTech Mining monitoring [https://im-mining.com/2021/09/17/cummins-preventech-mining-keeps-komatsu-trucks-wheel-loaders-going-at-boliden-mines/]. The PC4000-6 hydraulic mining shovel has a complete pre-heating system with engine coolant heating (KIM HOTSTART), engine oil reserve tank heater, engine-independent Hydronic cab heater with programmable start times, and battery/pre-heat main switches [https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3641219/Komatsu-Pc4000-6.html?page=151; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3641219/Komatsu-Pc4000-6.html?page=95].

### 1.3 Volvo CE

Volvo's articulated haulers (A25–A60) and large excavators (EC950F) carry **no OEM-published –40°C cold-start rating** in any materials reviewed. The A60 spec emphasizes coolant EGR, DOC, DPF, and SCR aftertreatment — all of which create cold-weather complications (DPF regeneration management; DEF freezing at –11°C) that Volvo's own cold-weather prep guide addresses but does not specifically solve for extreme cold [https://www.volvoce.com/united-states/en-us/products/articulated-haulers/a60/; https://www.volvoce.com/en-ca/discover/guides-and-advice/2021/diesel-engine-dos-and-donts-to-prep-for-winter-season/]. Volvo's articulated hauler concept is marketed on year-round utilization in adverse weather rather than extreme-cold certification. For a large mine needing 130–240 t rigid haul trucks, Volvo's only rigid hauler (R100E, 95 t) [https://www.engineering10.com/MN/Ulaanbaatar/104317184885421/Volvo-Mongolia] is too small.

### 1.4 BelAZ (Russian-bloc)

BelAZ has the broadest documented cold-rated product line in this comparison, all factory-rated **–50°C to +50°C**:

| Model | Payload | Engine | Cold Rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| BelAZ-75710 | 450 t | 2× MTU DD 16V4000 (Tier 1) | –50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-75605 | 360 t | 18-cyl, 3,300 hp | –50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-75306 | 220 t | Cummins QSK 60 | –50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-7513A | 130–136 t | MTU DD 12V4000 | –50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-7558B | 90 t | Cummins KTA 38-C (preheat) | –50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-7513R (robotic) | 130–136 t | electric drive | –50/+50°C |

Sources: [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/651/BELAZ_75710.pdf]; [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/d44/BELAZ_75306.pdf]; [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/3a9/BELAZ_7513A.pdf]; [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/5ce/BELAZ_7558_English.pdf]; [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/a29/_75605.pdf]; [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/589/BELAZ_7513R.pdf]. BelAZ specific fuel consumption at nominal power is 196–201 g/kWh (BelAZ-75710: 198; 75605: 196; 7513A: 201), competitive with Western diesel-electric drives (typically 190–200 g/kWh). BelAZ has also piloted LNG cryogenic fuel systems intended to reduce diesel dependence in Russian coal regions like Kuzbass [https://www.matec-conferences.org/articles/matecconf/pdf/2019/46/matecconf_ispcime18_03002.pdf].

### 1.5 Liebherr (European, with Russian Arctic Track Record)

Liebherr's R 9150 G7 mining excavator with the **Arctic Package** was validated at ALROSA's Udachny mine operating **–55°C to +40°C** with on-site 24/7 Liebherr service support [https://budmain.org.ua/upload/filescatalog/items/0/06aff05bd8ef30d68330e7a787c0.pdf; https://www.liebherr.com/en-int/mining-equipment/equipment/mining-excavators/r9150-5392635]. The PR 776 mining dozer operates 24/7 at Nornickel's Bystrinsky GOK in Siberia's Trans-Baikal Territory [https://www.liebherr.com/shared/media/mining/brochures/job-reports/pr-776-bystrinsky/job-report-pr-776-russia-bystrinsky-mine.pdf].

---

## 2. Local Service Centers in Ulaanbaatar

### 2.1 Caterpillar — Barloworld Mongolia

Barloworld Mongolia LLC (formerly Wagner Asia Equipment, est. 1996, 100% South African investment via Barloworld Limited; acquired by Barloworld Feb 2020 for $216.8M [https://im-mining.com/2020/02/04/barloworld-makes-plans-establish-eurasia-equipment-unit/]) was the best-performing Caterpillar dealer in the Eurasia/CIS region for **seven consecutive years** [http://www.mongolianbusinessdatabase.com/base/companydetials?id=3449; https://www.cbinsights.com/company/wagner-asia]. HQ: Bayangol District, Ulaanbaatar; branches in Zaamar (Tuv), Darkhan city, Tsogttsetsii, Khanbogd (Umnugovi — serving Oyu Tolgoi), and Zamiin-Uud (Dornogovi); ~600 employees [https://linkedin.com/company/barloworldmongolia; https://rocketreach.co/wagner-asia-equipment-llc-profile_b5c803a1f42e346e].

**UB main shop**: 975 m², 100+ mechanics + 20+ supervisors; field-service team for nationwide 24/7 dispatch with 50+ mechanics and 20+ delivery vehicles; 24/7 hotline; equipment includes two overhead cranes (3.2 T and 10 T), nine specialized service lifts (sized for 773, D9, 980, 390); 350 m² heavy-equipment wash bay; Cat contamination-control 4-Star certified; ISO 9001:2015 + OHSAS 18001:2007 accredited. The team has performed 70+ major rebuilds with 20+ years of mechanic tenure [https://www.barloworld.mn/en/service/main; https://www.barloworld.mn/en/service/field]. The Component Rebuild Center performs full rebuilds on torque converters, transmissions, differentials, wheel groups, gearboxes, cylinders, supported by new parts, Reman, parts kits, salvaged, repaired, and remanufactured components [https://www.barloworld.mn/en/service/component]. The Parts & Mining Division runs ~US$130 M/year across nine departments with 390 employees [https://linkedin.com/in/randy-adler-5594282b]. Authorized for Cat, SEM, Michelin, Trimble, Cat MineStar, Cat Product Link, S·O·S fluid analysis, and Trimble VisionLink.

### 2.2 Komatsu — Transwest Mongolia

Transwest Mongolia LLC holds exclusive Komatsu rights, backed by Sumitomo Corporation (Japan) and SMS Equipment (Canada). HQ: No. 30, Erchim Khuch Street 1, Bayangol District, 29th khoroo, Ulaanbaatar; +976-7575-9905 [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/about-us/]. Around 203 employees; revenue ~US$28.9M [https://rocketreach.co/transwest-mongolia-llc-profile_b5d8adf1f42e5ca4]. Komatsu itself opened a representative office (KLTD Ulaanbaatar) in 2025 in addition to Transwest's 15 years of presence [https://mn.linkedin.com/company/transwest-mongolia; https://www.bus-ex.com/article/transwest-mongolia-llc-forging-local-excellence-through-innovation-skills-green-technology].

**UB Component Rebuild shop** performs major/minor rebuilds for Komatsu and other brands: diesel engine and transmission overhauls, hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing, electrical component rebuild (motors, alternators, fan impellers, multistage pumps, electrical motor rotors). Undercarriage parts stocked at the UB parts warehouse, with track presses at the UB service center for pin-and-bushing turns [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/service-4a361fe3ec4f0cd803809746e23d4742/component-rebuild/; https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/parts-and-products/undercarriage/]. Service catalog documents 300+ component rebuilds, 50+ machine assemblies, and 200+ on-call services annually, with a second service facility commissioned in Khanbogd soum, Umnugovi province in 2022 (serving Oyu Tolgoi directly) [https://www.transwest.mn/getmedia/55fdc3ac-a9dc-473f-8e07-4dd02340b8e0/Service-Catalogue.pdf]. Welding/fabrication shop has line-boring, a 500-ton vertical press, and a 100-ton H-beam press [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/service-4a361fe3ec4f0cd803809746e23d4742/welding-and-machine-shop/].

### 2.3 Volvo CE — Effectively No Mining-Class Dealer

The research did not identify a clear, dedicated Volvo Construction Equipment dealership network in Mongolia for mining-class equipment. The Volvo CE global dealer locator lists Mongolia in its country dropdown but the dealer match page shows no dealer location for Mongolia [https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/global-dealer-locator/]. The only Volvo-branded entities found are:
- **Volvo Trucks Mongolia** (MNTTT Group, +976-7715-1534) — covers on-highway trucks, not mining excavators/haulers [https://www.volvotrucks.mn/en-mn/].
- **Volvo Mongolia** on Seoul Street, MGG Building — a small sales-office listing offering the R100E 95-t rigid hauler, described by one source as a sales/import arrangement rather than a full-service CE dealership [https://www.engineering10.com/MN/Ulaanbaatar/104317184885421/Volvo-Mongolia].
- A 2014 record of Volvo CE Region China delivering an EC220DLR to Inner Mongolia Liaoan Machinery (NMLA), a China-based dealer, not a Mongolian one [https://constructionshows.com/volvo-reaches-mongolia/].

A LinkedIn profile of a "Service & Workshop Manager, Volvo Industrial Equipment, Mongolia" active 2009–2011 [https://mn.linkedin.com/in/saimun-said-6796abb] suggests Volvo CE had some in-country presence a decade ago, but no current official mining-class dealer is verifiable. **Conclusion**: For a primary mining fleet, this is a disqualifying gap.

### 2.4 BelAZ — United BelAZ Machinery LLC

Three of four panels identify **United BelAZ Machinery LLC (UBM)** as the official BelAZ distributor in Mongolia since 2012, established specifically to resolve parts/service complaints from earlier grey imports [https://ikon.mn/n/272t]. UBM has ~160 employees (130 mining machinery engineers/technicians), a **2,289 m² UB service base** (re-certified 2020), generator/electric-motor repair shops, and centralized parts and tire warehouses in UB and Umnugovi valued at **16 billion MNT (~US$4.5M)**, with 24/7 support points at mine sites and Belarusian factory specialists (e.g., L.Ya. Slobodsky) permanently assigned to Mongolia [https://minprom.gov.by/belazy-serii-7513-budut-rabotat-v-pustyne-gobi/]. BelAZ has shipped trucks to Mongolia continuously since the 1970s, with about 200 BelAZ vehicles currently in operation across Erdenet and Tavan Tolgoi [https://www.belarus.by/en/business/business-news/belarusian-belaz-ships-first-bulldozer-to-mongolia_i_110184.html; https://eng.belta.by/economics/view/belaz-to-ship-3m-worth-of-haul-trucks-to-mongolia-103863-2017/].

---

## 3. Parts Inventory for Rapid Repairs

| Brand | Dealer | Documented Parts Capacity |
|---|---|---|
| Caterpillar | Barloworld Mongolia | ~36,000 SKUs / ~2.76 M units across four Mongolian branches, ISO 9001 + Cat Contamination Control [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/barloworldmongolia_partsavailability-reliability-operationalexcellence-activity-7455421923053740032-dal1]; parent network provides access to 1.4 M genuine Cat parts via Parts.cat.com [https://barloworld-equipment.com/parts]; full in-shop rebuild for torque converters, transmissions, differentials, wheel groups, gearboxes, cylinders |
| Komatsu | Transwest Mongolia | UB parts warehouse for undercarriage & OEM all-makes coverage + Track Management System + Track Press; exclusive distribution agreement for equipment, parts, service, component remanufacture, and rebuild [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/about-us/; https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/parts-and-products/undercarriage/]; Komatsu genuine and Reman parts via My Komatsu [https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/products/parts] |
| Volvo CE | None official | Third-party air-freight from Mumbai 5–7 days via DHL/FedEx [https://partstrading.com/suppliers/volvo-parts-mongolia/]; slower 14–28 days by sea; Chinese brokers reference Volvo model numbers EC140–EC900 [https://www.xmgtech.com/mn/volvo-model] |
| BelAZ | UBM | 16B MNT centralized UB + Umnugovi parts/tire warehouse; Belarus factory supply; 130 engineers/technicians [https://ikon.mn/n/272t] |

**Logistics warning for Mongolia**: Tianjin port congestion routinely strands ~6,000 containers with delays up to three months; logistics add **15–20%** to cost (Sandvik), ~12% of product cost (SMS/MSM), or up to 30% (ADB) [https://projects.gbreports.com/mongolia-mining-2024/equipment-and-technology-maturing-in-a-realm-of-unpredictability]. This favors whichever supplier holds the largest in-country inventory — currently Cat and Komatsu.

---

## 4. Fuel Efficiency in Extreme Cold

### 4.1 Diesel Penalty at –40°C

Fleet fuel economy drops materially in extreme cold because of increased warm-up time and fluid viscosity, tire pressure drops reducing rolling efficiency, increased aerodynamic drag (a 10°F drop raises drag ~2%, ~1% MPG loss per 2% drag increase) [https://www.freightliner.com/blog-and-newsletters/how-adverse-weather-affects-fuel-economy/], and winter-blend fuels (No. 1-D for cloud/pour-point control) have lower BTU content; No. 2-D clouds at ~+7°C (45°F) [https://restservice.epri.com/publicdownload/TR-104843/0/Product; https://www.atbs.com/post/diesel-winterization]. Light-duty vehicles lose ~15% MPG at –7°C (20°F) vs. 25°C (77°F), up to ~24% on short trips; heavy diesel on long runs drops ~5–10% in extreme cold, with frequent cold starts and idling making the effective impact much worse [https://www.elementfleet.com/insights-and-resources/insights/blogs/fleet-fuel-management-how-cold-temperatures-affect-fuel-economy].

**Mongolia-specific fuel context**: Mongolia imports approximately **95% of petroleum products from Russia**; Western sanctions on Russian banks and energy companies have created payment difficulties and supply uncertainty, complicating procurement of winter-grade (low-cloud-point) diesel for Ulaanbaatar and South Gobi operations [https://www.intellinews.com/hit-indirectly-by-sanctions-mongolia-struggles-to-find-workarounds-351043/; https://www.trtworld.com/asia/mongolia-is-feeling-weight-of-western-sanctions-on-russia-over-ukraine-war-18214964]. At –40°C, **arctic-grade diesel meeting GOST R 55475-2013 with limiting filtration temperature ≤ –44°C** is mandatory; standard winter grade (-32 or –38°C) will gel [https://meganorms.com/gost-r-55475-2013.html]. Mongolia holds ~85,600 t of national diesel reserves covering only ~21 days of consumption and is diversifying suppliers to China/South Korea via slow rail-gauge transfers [https://mn.ibtimes.com/mongolia-expands-fuel-supply-beyond-russia-china-south-korea-1812481]. Winterization of fuel (anti-gel additives, kerosene blending, fuel-blender preheaters) is therefore essential regardless of OEM.

### 4.2 Manufacturer-Specific Strategies

**Caterpillar** approach (per Cat spec sheets): eliminate cold idling with auto-warm-up, cold-start block heaters (Cat 395 rated –32°C/–25°F), arctic hydraulic oil, antifreeze down to –50°C/–58°F (Cat 824), and fuel blender/heater elements in the Cold Weather Package to keep wax crystals small and prevent fuel-filter icing [https://www.cat.com/en_US/products/new/equipment/excavators/large-excavators/126440.html; https://www.fabickcat.com/new-equipment/824-wheel-dozer/]. Cat 785 "Fuel Optimized" emissions ratings (outside North America) avoid Tier 4 SCR-DEF complexity [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20240909-c65b1-7536b] — eliminating DEF freezing and the 70-minute DEF thaw problem documented by Komatsu's own Tier 4 equivalent [https://www.constructionequipment.com/earthmoving/rigid-frame-trucks-off-highway/product/10752402/komatsu-komatsu-930e-5-haul-truck].

**Komatsu ThermaStart** autonomous idle management system on the 830E, field-tested through Canadian tundra at –30°C, eliminates unnecessary idling and warm-up cycles via continuous monitoring of block temperature, battery voltage, and air pressure; reportedly delivers ROI within days [https://www.roscomining.com/post/thermastart-komatsu-830e-cold-weather; https://www.roscomining.com/featured-projects]. For oil-sands/bitumen transport, the 980E-5 routes engine exhaust through the dump body to keep ore from freezing to the body, reducing wasted fuel on stuck-payload cleanup [https://www.komatsu.jp/en/-/media/home/aboutus/innovation/technology/techreport/2017/en/180330_06e.pdf]. The 930E-5 achieves up to 5% less fuel than its predecessor via on-demand cooling [https://www.constructionequipment.com/earthmoving/rigid-frame-trucks-off-highway/product/10752402/komatsu-komatsu-930e-5-haul-truck]; the AC electric drive is documented as "more efficient, offers better operating characteristics and is more cost-effective than a comparable DC powertrain" [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komatsu_930E].

**Volvo CE**: operator guidance is to drain fuel/water separators nightly, fill fuel tanks nightly (reduces condensation), regenerate DPF before cold shutdown, swap to arctic-grade engine/hydraulic oils; Volvo's V-ACT D16J on the A60 claims "up to 15% more fuel efficiency" vs. prior generation [https://www.volvoce.com/en-ca/discover/guides-and-advice/2021/diesel-engine-dos-and-donts-to-prep-for-winter-season/; https://www.volvoce.com/united-states/en-us/products/articulated-haulers/a60/]. Volvo EC350E claims up to 9% better fuel efficiency than its prior generation [https://www.volvoce.com/united-states/en-us/products/excavators/ec350e/] — paper gains that would erode at –40°C without local support to validate them in Mongolian service.

**BelAZ**: SFC at nominal power is 196–201 g/kWh, competitive with modern Western diesel-electric drives (190–200 g/kWh), though fuel efficiency at partial load / cold ambient is not separately published. BelAZ has piloted LNG cryogenic fuel systems for Kuzbass to reduce diesel dependence [https://www.matec-conferences.org/articles/matecconf/pdf/2019/46/matecconf_ispcime18_03002.pdf].

### 4.3 Measured Outcomes from Mongolian Operations

- **Erdenet Mining Corporation**: after introducing Komatsu HD1500-8 (142 t, ~18 in fleet), rock haulage volume increased **7.9%** and cost per m³ decreased **5.8%** [https://erdenettoday.mn/art/7169]. The HD1500-8 fleet has accumulated ~16,000 operating hours over two years on the first 10 delivered in Dec 2024 [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/transwest-mongolia_komatsu-komatsuhd1500-hd1500-activity-7500022394456092672-Wf2J].
- **Oyu Tolgoi**: 28× Komatsu 930E-4SE operational at 1,300 m altitude in the South Gobi since August 2012, with 90+ female operators [https://en.eot.mn/open-pit-mine; https://www.linkedin.com/posts/austcham-mongolia_transwest-mongolia-activity-7416752742452506624-0yVm].
- **Tavan Tolgoi**: 17× BelAZ-75135 (130 t) climate-configured delivered [https://minprom.gov.by/belazy-serii-7513-budut-rabotat-v-pustyne-gobi/].
- All nominal efficiency gains will be partially eroded at –40°C by idle-heating and cab-heat loads; treat vendor fuel guarantees as temperate-climate numbers.

---

## 5. Operator Training Programs for Mongolian Workers

### 5.1 Caterpillar / Barloworld Mongolia

Caterpillar's Mining Technology Academy (MTA) [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20250714-13ab0-e7282] offers eLearning, Instructor-Led Training (ILT), and three operator levels (Level I entry, Level II efficiency for 3+ years, Competent Operator evaluation) [https://www.catoperatortraining.com/pages/instructor-led-training; https://www.cat.com/en_US/support/cat-training/operator-training.html]. Web-based eLearning covers safety, controls, maintenance, and inspection [https://www.cat.com/en_US/support/cat-training/operator-training/operator-elearning.html]. Barloworld Mongolia runs an in-country training department with accredited Caterpillar instructors (e.g., Batbayar Dorjsuren) [https://linkedin.com/in/batbayar-dorjsuren-161b51b9] and staff attend Caterpillar's Tinaja Hills Demonstration & Learning Center for MineStar Terrain/product training [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nymbaatar-altansukh-a86b59199_caterpillar-minestar-minestarterrain-activity-7473644063595048960-kdc9].

Historical benchmark: the **Wagner Training Institute (WTI)**, established ~2001, ran an apprentice program with ~30 students per intake, ~150 Mongolian technicians trained across six intakes in five years in partnership with the Mongolian-Korean Technical College; **100% graduate employment** [https://news.mn/en/12137/; https://wagnerequipment.com/wagner-training-institute/wti-staff/]. Customers send mechanics on paid 10-month theory+practice courses (e.g., Energy Resources for the Ukhaa Khudag mine) [https://en.energyresources.mn/post/179240].

### 5.2 Komatsu / Transwest Mongolia Technical Institute (TMTI)

TMTI delivers Mongolia's most localized, structured workforce-development pipeline. In February 2026 TMTI delivered advanced hydraulic-systems training on Komatsu 930E-4SE electric-drive dump trucks to Oyu Tolgoi's Heavy Equipment Maintenance Department in combined classroom and practical format, in Mongolian and English [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/transwest-mongolia_komatsu930e-oyutolgoillc-komatsu930e-activity-7428957197641895936-Bo-1]. In June–July 2025 Transwest co-delivered Komatsu PC7000-11D Technical Training with Komatsu Germany Mining (KGM) at Nariin Sukhait Mine — 10-day combined program [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/chinzorig-ganbat_were-proud-to-announce-the-successful-completion-activity-7355832096709337089-e_Gv]. Transwest's training program integrates Australian curriculum (via SMS Equipment Canada), Komatsu training systems, and locally designed modules [https://www.bus-ex.com/article/transwest-mongolia-llc-forging-local-excellence-through-innovation-skills-green-technology]. Komatsu Academy offers self-paced online modules and instructor-led live coaching [https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/services-and-support/training-programs].

### 5.3 Immersive Technologies / Oyu Tolgoi Simulation

Oyu Tolgoi invested in the PRO3 simulator from Immersive Technologies in 2011 for Komatsu haul-truck operator training, with a five-year gold support program and Custom Mine Site [https://www.immersivetechnologies.com/news/news2011/news_2011_21.htm]. Oyu Tolgoi also runs the largest vocational training program ever established in Mongolia.

### 5.4 Mongolia Polytechnic / German-Mongolian Cooperation (2025)

A "Mining Machinery Operation Technician" program at the Polytechnic College affiliated with the University of Technology in Ömnögovi province is delivered via public-private partnership with Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. More than 80% of students are from Umnögovi, with blended learning and learn-while-working placements at mining employers [https://mcpg.mn/en/9281/].

### 5.5 South Gobi Underground Mass Mining Institute (2025)

Launched in March 2025 by Rio Tinto and the University of Queensland, based at Oyu Tolgoi with a 2025 cohort of 28 participants; 2026 curriculum will open to local and international mining companies [https://www.australianmining.com.au/rio-tinto-debuts-world-class-training-program-at-oyu-tolgoi/].

### 5.6 Volvo CE

No Mongolia-specific mining operator program identified. Volvo CE's general Machine Operator Training combines classroom theory and practical field instruction [https://www.volvoce.com/asia/services/machine-operator-training/], but would require regional travel (China/South Korea) or traveling instructors.

### 5.7 BelAZ

United BelAZ Machinery sends Mongolian specialists to the BelAZ factory in Zhodino, Belarus, for operations and service training, with documented training groups returning from Zhodino [https://news.mn/en/135983/], complementing its 130 Mongolian engineers/technicians. Curriculum is BelAZ-specific.

---

## 6. Russian-Made and CIS Alternatives

### 6.1 Regional Trade Context

- Mongolia imports roughly 28% of goods from Russia and depends on Russia for **~95% of petroleum products** [https://www.trtworld.com/asia/mongolia-is-feeling-weight-of-western-sanctions-on-russia-over-ukraine-war-18214964].
- December 2024 saw an interim trade agreement between the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and Mongolia [https://russiancouncil.ru/en/analytics-and-comments/analytics/russia-and-mongolia-forging-stronger-trade-relations/]; February 2026 saw further expansion via Mongolia-Russia Business Forum (70+ Mongolian and 100+ Russian businesses) [https://thediplomat.com/2026/02/with-speaker-uchrals-trip-mongolia-and-russia-look-to-expand-economic-links/].
- However, US/EU sanctions on Russia have created indirect payment difficulties for Mongolia, secondary-sanction risk deterring direct air links, and parts-supply delays via banks and logistics chains [https://www.intellinews.com/hit-indirectly-by-sanctions-mongolia-struggles-to-find-workarounds-351043/; https://iz.ru/en/node/1848658].
- For BelAZ specifically, no direct sanctions impact on BelAZ was identified, but the broader Russia-CIS logistics environment is uncertain and Mongolian buyers reportedly fear secondary-sanction exposure when transacting with Russian counterparties.
- China dominates Mongolia's construction-machinery import market at **65–70% by value** (2026), with Japanese OEMs (Komatsu, Hitachi) holding the large mining segment and second-hand imports at ~20% [https://www.ibicrossborder.com/upload/ai_report/en/html/20260718003522-f2bb78fbbc.html]. BelAZ holds ~30% of global ultra-class (>100 t) mining haul truck market [https://eec.eaeunion.org/upload/iblock/c35/uwfzw97f600k4kof5yi9t1xpk4wrzc1v/review_mining.pdf].
- Fixed mining equipment market top-five (Metso, Sandvik, FLSmidth, Caterpillar, Weir) collectively hold ~65% of revenue (2026), with Komatsu and others in second tier [https://www.marknteladvisors.com/research-library/mongolia-fixed-mining-equipment-market.html].

### 6.2 BelAZ Haul Trucks

The strongest evidence in this study for genuine –40°C capability comes from BelAZ across its –50/+50°C rated line (75710 450 t, 75605 360 t, 75306 220 t, 7513A 130–136 t, 7558B 90 t, plus robotic 7513R). BelAZ has supplied Mongolia since the 1970s; about 200 units currently operating at Erdenet (30, 45, 55, 130 t classes) and Tavan Tolgoi (Gobi-climate configured 75135) [https://eng.belta.by/economics/view/belaz-to-ship-3m-worth-of-haul-trucks-to-mongolia-103863-2017/]. Pricing per 130-tonne truck is reported in Panel 2 at ~US$1M, substantially below Cat/Komatsu ultra-class equivalents.

**BelAZ strengths**: lower unit cost; proven in Mongolia across decades; factory –50°C rating as standard; UBM 16B MNT parts warehouse; shortest logistics chain among heavy-truck OEMs for landlocked Mongolia; logistics more insulated from Western geopolitical disruption than US/Japan supply chains.

**BelAZ weaknesses**: no comparable Cat MineStar Command/Komatsu FrontRunner autonomous hauling; no real-time digital fleet management comparable to Cat Product Link/KOMTRAX; generally higher fuel per tonne-km than Western/Japanese equivalents; cab ergonomics notably inferior; global service network limited outside CIS; sanctions risk on Western engine sourcing (Cummins KTA38-C, MTU DD 16V4000) means newer models may shift to Russian engines with lower performance.

### 6.3 UZTM-KARTEX (Russia) — Mining Excavators

UZTM-KARTEX (Uralmashzavod–IZ-KARTEKS) manufactures electric rope shovels and, more recently, hydraulic excavators.

- **EKG-12K** — 12 m³ bucket, proven in Mongolia at Erdenet Mining Corporation. UZTM-KARTEX resumed direct supplies to Erdenet in 2018 to replace end-of-life units; four EKG-12K delivered by 2020 [https://www.eanews.ru/ekaterinburg/20200629115534/uztm-karteks-postavit-ekskavatory-v-mongoliyu]. Erdenet expects a 30% productivity increase and 20% cost reduction with EKG-12K vs. older models.
- **EKG-20KM northern variant (EKG-20KM-KhL)** — rated for operation down to **–60°C**, using special steel grades tested for impact toughness at –50°C, arctic-grade greases, cold-rated electrical components [https://mashnews.ru/na-kovdorskom-goke-montiruyut-novyij-otechestvennyij-ekskavator-ekg-20km-s-kovshom-obemom-20-kubometrov.html] — the most extreme cold rating of any manufacturer in this comparison.
- **EKG-35** — 35 m³ bucket, 1,250 tonnes, paired with 220–320 t trucks.
- **BELAZ BX20012** — BelAZ's first excavator (12 m³ bucket, 214 t, 1,150 hp diesel), recently delivered to Siberian coal mines — a new CIS hydraulic-excavator entrant.

**UZTM-KARTEX strengths**: extreme –60°C northern-variant rating; Mongolian familiarity via Erdenet; significantly cheaper than Western/Japanese equivalents; electric drive on EKG-series eliminates diesel concerns entirely at extreme temperatures when grid power is available.

**UZTM-KARTEX weaknesses**: primarily rope shovels with nascent hydraulic excavator offerings; cannot match full Cat/Komatsu hydraulic mining shovel range (Cat 6015–6060; Komatsu PC3000–PC8000); lower automation/telematics/digital integration; service network in Mongolia limited compared to Barloworld/Transwest.

### 6.4 Russian-Engine Sourcing Sanctions Risk

Since 2022, Western sanctions have complicated the supply chain for BelAZ and UZTM-KARTEX. BelAZ trucks use Cummins and MTU engines (e.g., BelAZ-75131 uses Cummins KTA50-C [https://belaz.by/en/press-centre/time-tested-130-ton-heroes-of-the-arctic/]; BelAZ-75302 uses MTU DD 16V4000 or Cummins QSK60-C [https://img.forconstructionpros.com/files/base/acbm/fcp/document/2024/5/7530.html]) — sourcing these Western engines has become harder under sanctions, and newer BelAZ models may shift to Russian engines with lower performance. Mongolia maintains neutral diplomatic relations, but sanctions compliance may be required for equipment financed by international banks or used at mines with Western corporate ownership (e.g., Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi).

## 8. Final Recommendations for a –40°C Mongolia Mining Fleet

1. **Primary haul trucks**: Specify Komatsu 930E-5/930E-5SE (290–320 t) and Cat 793F (240 t) with full cold-weather packages (coolant to –50°C, 220–240V coolant/oil/hydraulic pre-heaters, radiator shutters, cold-weather suspensions, heated-body exhaust on 980E-5). Both have proven Mongolian fleets — Komatsu 930E is dominant at Oyu Tolgoi (28+ trucks since 2012; 90+ female operators) [https://en.eot.mn/open-pit-mine]; Cat 793 combines with Barloworld's 36,000-SKU inventory. Consider Komatsu HD1500-8 (142 t, ~18 in Erdenet fleet) for mid-size operations [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/transwest-mongolia_komatsu-komatsuhd1500-hd1500-activity-7500022394456092672-Wf2J]. Specify non-emissionized or Fuel Optimized engine ratings to avoid DEF (which freezes at –11°C) and its 70-minute thaw penalty [https://www.constructionequipment.com/earthmoving/rigid-frame-trucks-off-highway/product/10752402/komatsu-komatsu-930e-5-haul-truck].

2. **Primary excavators**: Cat 6060/6040 or Komatsu PC2000/PC4000/PC7000 with factory Cold Weather Package (coolant/oil/hydraulic heaters, cab pre-heater, ~50 kW shore power). Cat 6040 cold-weather package documentation is the most detailed found [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20260211-22a73-3be06]; Komatsu PC4000's HYDRONIC independent cab heater is a genuine operational advantage for –40°C shift starts [https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3641219/Komatsu-Pc4000-6.html?page=95]. **Exclude Volvo CE from the primary mining fleet absent direct Mongolia dealer support with bonded parts warehouse** [https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/global-dealer-locator/; https://partstrading.com/suppliers/volvo-parts-mongolia/].

3. **Cost-effective / auxiliary haulage**: BelAZ-7558B (90 t), BelAZ-7513A (130 t), or BelAZ-75306 (220 t) for cost-driven auxiliary haul capacity or fleet diversification. UBM provides 16B MNT local parts warehouse and ~130 engineers [https://ikon.mn/n/272t]. Best paired with a Western service partner for high-value powertrain/hydraulic rebuilds given BelAZ's Mongolia service limitations in high-value components.

4. **Rope shovels (grid-powered)**: UZTM-KARTEX EKG-20KM-KhL northern variant (–60°C rated) [https://mashnews.ru/na-kovdorskom-goke-montiruyut-novyij-otechestvennyij-ekskavator-ekg-20km-s-kovshom-obemom-20-kubometrov.html] at Erdenet where grid power is available; eliminates diesel cold-start concerns entirely. EKG-12K already proven at Erdenet [https://www.eanews.ru/ekaterinburg/20200629115534/uztm-karteks-postavit-ekskavatory-v-mongoliyu].

5. **Support fleet**: Volvo articulated haulers (A40G/A60H) and excavators (EC480E-EC950E) can be considered for off-road support material transport where rigid haul trucks are oversized, but only with negotiated direct-support agreement with Volvo CE China regional office and on-site critical-spares stocking.

6. **Cold-weather engineering & fuel**: Mandate engine coolant/oil/hydraulic preheaters (Cat and Komatsu arctic packages), use arctic-grade fluids (Cat –50°C antifreeze confirmed on the 824 Wheel Dozer), integrate ThermaStart-like idle management, and pre-blend fuel with anti-gel additives. Mongolia imports 95% of diesel from Russia; secure **arctic-grade diesel meeting GOST R 55475-2013 with limiting filtration temperature ≤ –44°C** (grade А) [https://meganorms.com/gost-r-55475-2013.html]. Budget external 400V three-phase shore power at the fleet parking area to energize the ~50 kW pre-heating systems overnight — the single largest lever on cold-start reliability and fuel economy.

7. **Training**: Build on Transwest Mongolia Technical Institute + Barloworld Mining Technology Academy + Wagner Training Institute pathways. Partner with Rio Tinto's South Gobi Underground Mass Mining Institute (2025 cohort 28 participants) [https://www.australianmining.com.au/rio-tinto-debuts-world-class-training-program-at-oyu-tolgoi/] and the Ömnögovi Polytechnic "Mining Machinery Operation Technician" program for the long-term workforce pipeline [https://mcpg.mn/en/9281/].

8. **Spare-parts SLA**: Negotiate consignment-stock contracts with Barloworld Mongolia and Transwest Mongolia for the highest-failure-rate SKUs (hydraulic hoses, undercarriage components, fuel/water separator elements, coolant hoses). Mongolia's landlocked logistics and 15–30% logistics-cost adders [https://projects.gbreports.com/mongolia-mining-2024/equipment-and-technology-maturing-in-a-realm-of-unpredictability] make any 5–7-day air-freight cycle (Volvo path) unacceptable for primary mining-truck downtime.

## 9. Key Uncertainties

# The State of Deepfake Detection Research Since 2022

Since 2022, deepfake detection has shifted from a niche forensic concern into a mainstream sociotechnical problem. Between 2023 and 2024, the number of deepfakes detected in fraud cases rose approximately fourfold, and an estimated 500,000 deepfakes were shared on social media in 2023 alone (Chandra et al., 2025; https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02857v4). Generation moved from GAN-dominated face-swapping to diffusion models (Stable Diffusion), talking-head systems, and commercial voice cloning (ElevenLabs, etc.), fundamentally changing the artifact statistics detectors must learn.

---

## 1. Video Detection Methods

### 1.1 CNN and Spatial Baselines
XceptionNet remains the de facto CNN baseline; it scored AUC 0.997 trained and tested on FaceForensics++ (FF++) but collapsed to 0.482 when transferred to Celeb-DF (Nadimpalli et al., CVPRW 2022; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022W/WMF/papers/Nadimpalli_On_Improving_Cross-Dataset_Generalization_of_Deepfake_Detectors_CVPRW_2022_paper.pdf), an absolute drop of 0.515 (~52% relative degradation). Frequency-domain methods like F3-Net achieved 97.52% accuracy on FF++ (HQ) but only 57.87% AUC when transferred to DFDC (https://netinfo-security.org/EN/10.36969/j.issn.1671-1122.2024.08.004). RECCE (Cao et al., CVPR 2022) introduced end-to-end reconstruction-classification learning (https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2022/supplemental/Cao_End-to-End_Reconstruction-Classification_Learning_CVPR_2022_supplemental.pdf).

### 1.2 Transformer-Based Architectures
A 2024 systematic review catalogued 14 ViT-based detectors (Khan et al., https://arxiv.org/html/2405.08463) and reported that transformer-based architectures exhibit only ~11.33% cross-dataset performance decline, compared with >15% for CNN-based methods, though at 3–5× higher computational cost (https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/7/2/68). Representative results:
- **UIA-ViT (2022)**: AUC 99.33 on FF++ (HQ); cross-dataset AUC 94.68 (DFD), 82.41 (Celeb-DF-v2), 75.80 (DFDC).
- **ISTVT (2023)**: 99.0% accuracy on FF++ (HQ), 99.8% on Celeb-DF, 92.1% on DFDC.
- **M2TR (2022)**: AUC 99.51 (FF++ HQ), 99.92 (FF++ RAW), 95.5 (Celeb-DF), 86.7 (SR-DF).
- **FA-ViT** (arXiv:2309.11092): 93.83% AUC on Celeb-DF and 78.32% AUC on DFDC cross-dataset evaluation (https://arxiv.org/html/2309.11092).
- **DualFocusNet**: trained on DFDC-p, 82.5% AUC on FF++, 86.2% on Celeb-DF, 87.3% on DeeperForensics, 82.0% on WildDeepfake (https://exa.ai/library/publication/hk6myvz0wzc).
- **ICT**: AUC 90.22% (FF++), 93.57% (DeeperForensics), 85.71% (Celeb-DFv2), 84.13% (DFD) (https://arxiv.org/html/2405.08463).
- **DeepFake-Adapter**: the first parameter-efficient tuning approach for deepfake detection (https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00863).

### 1.3 Diffusion-Model and Universal Image Forensics
Ricker et al. (2024; https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2024/124220/124220.pdf) showed state-of-the-art GAN detectors fail on diffusion-generated images, but re-training them on diffusion images yields near-perfect detection that generalizes back to GANs. Recent universal detectors include:
- **ZED** (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15875): 3%+ average accuracy improvement over prior SOTA across many generators, zero AI-generated training data required.
- **TSG** (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.11016v2): uses pre-trained diffusion network as feature extractor with varying time steps.
- **APN** (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1016/j.cviu.2024.104078): 5.6–16.4% higher accuracy on GenImage and 1.7–50.1% on DiffusionForensics.
- **Community Forensics** (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04125v1): 2.7M images from 4,803 generators; detector generalization scales with quantity and diversity of generators.

---

## 2. Audio Detection Methods

### 2.1 End-to-End Architectures
**AASIST** (Jung et al., arXiv:2110.01200) uses a heterogeneous stacking graph attention layer with a max graph operation; even AASIST-L with only 85K parameters outperformed all competing systems on ASVspoof 2019 LA (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.01200v1). **RawNet2** ingests raw waveforms via SincNet filters (https://mm.kaist.ac.kr/pubs/pdfs/jung22c.pdf). Improvements since 2022:
- **ARawNet2** (Li et al., Interspeech 2023): attention-based channel masking; EER 4.61% on ASVspoof 2019 LA, 8.36% on 2021 LA, 19.03% on 2021 DF (https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2023/li23h_interspeech.pdf).
- **TO-RawNet** (Interspeech 2023): 66.09% relative EER reduction on ASVspoof 2019 LA (https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2023/wang23w_interspeech.pdf).

### 2.2 Self-Supervised Front-Ends
The dominant post-2022 paradigm pairs SSL backbones with lightweight heads:
- **wav2vec 2.0 + augmentation** (arXiv:2202.12233): pretrained only on bona fide data; achieved lowest EERs on ASVspoof 2021 LA and DF, ~90% relative improvement over baseline (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2202.12233).
- **Frozen SSL + logistic regression** (arXiv:2309.05384): <2k parameters reduced EER from 30.9% (RawNet2) to 8.8% across eight deepfake datasets — a 71.5% relative reduction (https://arxiv.org/html/2309.05384v2).
- **Whisper+AASIST** (HCII 2024): 2.85% EER on ASVspoof 2021 DF; on in-the-wild data, 24.73% EER (vs. 34.81% for vanilla AASIST) (https://faculty.cs.gwu.edu/xiaodongqu/papers/HCII_2024_572_Whisper_Qian.pdf).

### 2.3 ASVspoof 5 Challenge (2024)
ASVspoof 5 (Wang et al., https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08739v1) introduced crowdsourced data, neural codecs, and adversarial attacks. It replaced EER with minDCF as the primary Track 1 metric. Reported results:
- **ParallelChain Lab**: minDCF 0.2660 on Track 1 closed condition (https://www.isca-archive.org/asvspoof_2024/tran24_asvspoof.pdf).
- **USTC-KXDIGIT**: 0.3948 minDCF / 14.33% EER (Track 1 closed); 0.0750 minDCF / 2.59% EER (Track 1 open) (https://www.isca-archive.org/asvspoof_2024/chen24_asvspoof.pdf).
- **Fraunhofer SIT**: minDCF 0.589 closed, 0.174 open (SSL) (https://www.isca-archive.org/asvspoof_2024/schafer24_asvspoof.pdf).
- **SHADOW FwSE-ResNet34 with codec augmentation**: minDCF 0.44 (Track 1 Eval, 47% improvement); a-DCF 0.397 (Track 2, 42% improvement) (https://www.isca-archive.org/asvspoof_2024/villalba24_asvspoof.pdf).
- **AASIST3 with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks**: minDCF 0.5357 closed / 0.1414 open on ASVspoof 5 (https://www.isca-archive.org/asvspoof_2024/borodin24_asvspoof.pdf).

A WavLM ensemble reached 6.56%/17.07% EER on the two evaluation sets (https://arxiv.org/html/2408.07414v1), illustrating how sensitive headline numbers are to subset choice. Organizers concluded: "performance degrades under adversarial attacks and the application of neural encoding/compression schemes."

### 2.4 Cross-Domain Audio and ADD Challenges
**CD-ADD** (EMNLP 2024) built 300+ hours from five zero-shot TTS models with nine attack types; Wav2Vec2-large reached 4.1% EER and Whisper-medium 6.5% EER with attack augmentation (https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.286.pdf). **ADD 2022** Track 1 best EER was 21.7% across 48 submissions; ADD 2023 introduced manipulation localization and algorithm recognition, with top WEER 12.45% (https://arxiv.org/html/2202.08433v3; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.13774).

---

## 3. Cross-Dataset Generalization

Cross-dataset generalization is the field's central unsolved problem. Models suffer a 10–15% AUC decline across all methodological classes on academic benchmarks, with strong evidence that they "learn dataset-specific compression artifacts rather than deepfake characteristics that are generalizable" (https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/7/2/68).

Key approaches since 2022:
- **ED4** (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.06779): ClockMix facial-structure-preserved mixing + Adversarial Spatial Consistency Module to address content, forgery, and spatial bias.
- **D³ (Discrepancy Deepfake Detector)** (https://arxiv.org/html/2404.04584v1): parallel branch on distorted inputs; 5.3% accuracy improvement in OOD testing while maintaining ID performance.
- **GM-DF** (https://arxiv.org/html/2406.20078): hybrid expert modeling with CLIP-based common feature alignment across domains.
- **DFFC** (https://arxiv.org/html/2410.11162): Dynamic Facial Forensic Curriculum with Dynamic Forensic Hardness measure.
- **SoK paper** (https://arxiv.org/html/2401.04364v4): reviewed 51 detectors (2019–2023), built first white-box dataset, evaluated 16 SOTA detectors under black/gray/white-box conditions.

Kamat et al. (ICCVW 2023; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2023W/DFAD/papers/Kamat_Revisiting_Generalizability_in_Deepfake_Detection_Improving_Metrics_and_Stabilizing_Transfer_ICCVW_2023_paper.pdf) found methods fail differently depending on their trained artifact mode: on diffusion fakes, spatial/temporal/lip-reading methods scored 96%/75%/51% AUC; on talking-head fakes, the same scored 80%/99%/92%.

**DF40** (NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks; https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13495) contains 40 distinct deepfake techniques (10× FF++ diversity), millions of images/videos, and 4 evaluation protocols. The benchmark authors argue the *dataset*, not the algorithm, is "the primary culprit" for the generalization gap, because FF++ contains forgery techniques four years out of date.

---

## 4. Multimodal Audio-Visual Detection

- **AVFF** (Oorloff et al., CVPR 2024; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Oorloff_AVFF_Audio-Visual_Feature_Fusion_for_Video_Deepfake_Detection_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf): two-stage self-supervised learning on real videos via contrastive + autoencoding with complementary masking; 98.6% accuracy / 99.1% AUC on FakeAVCeleb (+14.9%/+9.9% over prior SOTA).
- **AVA-CL** (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3625100): joint audio-visual attention with contrastive learning using MARLIN face representations.
- **AV-Deepfake1M** (Cai et al., ACM MM 2024, Best Award; https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3664647.3680795): 2,000+ subjects, 1M+ videos for temporal localization of small manipulated segments; baseline AP@0.5 values extremely low (Meso4: 9.86, PyAnnote: 0.03).
- **SpeechForensics** (NeurIPS 2024; https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/9c7900fac04a701cbed83256b76dbaa3-Paper-Conference.pdf): self-supervised masked-prediction on real videos; outperforms SOTA on cross-dataset generalization without using any fake video in training.
- **AV-LGNN** (ACM MM 2024; https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3664647.3688985): Audio-Visual Local-Global Interaction Module.
- **MFMS** (ACM MM 2024; https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3664647.3688984): top performance in AV-Deepfake1M competition.
- **MSOC** (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.14176): multi-stream fusion with one-class learning on four FakeAVCeleb splits.
- **CAD** (https://arxiv.org/html/2505.15233): modality-shared semantic alignment + modality-specific forensic verification via cross-modal distillation.

---

## 5. Foundation Model Integration

CLIP-based adaptation has become the dominant direction since 2023:
- **CLIPping the Deception** (Khan & Dang-Nguyen, ICMR 2024; https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12927): prompt tuning on CLIP with 200k images (vs. 720k baseline); +5.01% mAP / +6.61% accuracy over prior SOTA, evaluated across 21 datasets.
- **C2P-CLIP** (https://arxiv.org/html/2408.09647v2): category-common prompts injected into CLIP text encoder; +12.41% accuracy over vanilla CLIP, no extra inference parameters.
- **Forensics Adapter** (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.19715v3): only 5.7M trainable parameters; ~7% average improvement across five datasets.
- **CLIPMoLE** (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.04883): fine-tunes 0.08% of parameters with mixture-of-LoRAs experts; +3.64% mAP / +12.72% avg accuracy.
- **Raising the Bar** (Cozzolino et al., CVPRW 2024; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024W/WMF/papers/Cozzolino_Raising_the_Bar_of_AI-generated_Image_Detection_with_CLIP_CVPRW_2024_paper.pdf): with handful of example images from one model, +6% AUC OOD and +13% robustness to impaired data.
- **RINE** (ECCV 2024; https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2024/papers_ECCV/papers/09160.pdf): intermediate CLIP block representations; +10.6% absolute improvement across 20 datasets with ~8 minutes training.
- **GenD** (https://arxiv.org/html/2508.06248v4): fine-tunes only Layer Normalization parameters (0.03% of total); enforces hyperspherical feature manifold via L2 normalization; SOTA across 14 benchmarks (2019–2025). Finds training on *paired* real-fake data from the same source video is essential.
- **Wavelet-CLIP** (https://arxiv.org/html/2409.18301v3): average AUC 0.749 cross-data / 0.893 unseen deepfakes.
- **Facial Component Guidance** (https://arxiv.org/html/2404.05583v2): CLIP image encoder + side-network decoder; +0.9% AUROC cross-dataset, +4.4% on DFDC.
- **AdaptPrompt** (https://arxiv.org/html/2512.17730): visual adapter + learnable text prompts (~0.1% trainable parameters); 98.60% mAP / 92.72% accuracy across 25 test sets.
- **M²F²-Det** (https://arxiv.deeppaper.ai/papers/2503.20188v1): CLIP + LLM for detection and textual justification.

Multimodal LLMs evaluated on 60,000-image deepfake datasets found "zero-shot VLMs superior to almost all existing methods" (https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22469), but a separate benchmark of 12 MLLMs found "the rest of the LLM families perform extremely disappointingly, with some worse than random guess" (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.20084).

---

## 6. Privacy-Preserving Techniques

Federated learning has emerged as the dominant paradigm:
- **FedForgery** (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.09563): VAE for residual feature maps + generalized FL.
- **Dynamic-Aware FL** (ACM TIST 2022; https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3501814): first FL for face-forgery *video* detection; Inconsistency-Capture Module with global/local inter-frame branches.
- **Blockchain-based FL** (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12559-024-10255-7): SegCaps + CNN with capsule training; +6.6% accuracy and +5.1% AUC over six benchmarks.
- **FL-TENB4** (https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/d97c/1fd280a818f9a30435c07717effc18a1cc08.pdf): Tiny EfficientNetB4-Lite for CCTV edge deployment.
- **FedMaxAdapt** (https://researchonline.gcu.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/113968862/113434712.pdf): adaptive sparsity; reduces bandwidth 43.1% (video) / 40.3% (audio) at 50% sparsity; 90.1% video / 91.0% audio accuracy.
- **FLADD** (https://eurekamag.com/research/110/713/110713846.php): dual-branch Res2Net + Rawformer with dual-prototype strategy; EER 0.285% on ASVspoof 2019 LA, 2.045% on 2021 LA.
- **SecDFDNet** (Digital Signal Processing, 2023; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1051200423003287): first privacy-preserving deepfake detection using additive secret sharing; secure protocols for non-linear activations (SecReLU, SecSigm, SecSpatial, SecChannel) with proven security; achieves plaintext DFDNet accuracy while revealing nothing of private inputs.

---

## 7. Benchmark vs. Real-World Deployment

The single most consequential finding of 2024–2025 is the magnitude of the benchmark-to-deployment gap.

**Deepfake-Eval-2024** (Chandra et al., CVPRW; https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02857v4) collected 45 hours of video, 56.5 hours of audio, and 1,975 images from 88 websites in 52 languages:

| Modality | Model | Original AUC | DF-Eval-2024 AUC | Drop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Video | GenConViT | 0.96 | 0.63 | ~34% |
| Video | FTCN | 0.87 | 0.50 | ~37% |
| Video | Styleflow | 0.95 | 0.51 | ~44% |
| Audio | AASIST | 1.00 | 0.43 | ~57% |
| Audio | RawNet2 | 0.99 | 0.53 | ~46% |
| Audio | P3 | 1.00 | 0.58 | ~42% |
| Image | UFD | 0.94 | 0.56 | ~38% |
| Image | DistilDIRE | 0.99 | 0.52 | ~47% |
| Image | NPR | 0.98 | 0.53 | ~45% |

Aggregate AUC drops: ~50% video, ~48% audio, ~45% image. Fine-tuning on 60% of DF-Eval-2024 yields 61–69% open-source accuracy; the best commercial detector reaches 82% — still below human forensic analysts.

**Corroborating evidence:**
- **SumSubstance** (https://arxiv.org/html/2507.21905): on 500,000+ high-quality deepfake images, fewer than half of tested detectors achieved AUC > 60%; JPEG compression causes further large drops.
- **arXiv:2509.04150**: better-tuned CLIP-based baseline achieves 81% accuracy on DF-Eval-2024, matching commercial systems.
- **arXiv:2511.07009**: models trained on contemporary deepfakes suffer >30% recall drop on deepfakes generated six months later — a quantitative statement of concept drift.
- **VendorBench-100** (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.06254v2): 36 models under edge-case conditions; commercial APIs strongest, followed by vision-LLMs; strong correlation (Pearson r ≈ 0.86) between MCC and ROC-AUC.
- **"How well are open sourced AI-generated image detection models out-of-the-box"** (https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07814): 37-percentage-point gap separates best (75.0%) from worst (37.5%); modern commercial generators (Flux Dev, Firefly v4, Midjourney v7) defeat most detectors (18–30% avg accuracy).
- **arXiv:2510.08067** (RedFace): 60,000 forged images from 9 commercial platforms; existing detectors fail to generalize.
- **"The Deployment Gap in AI Media Detection"** (CVPRW 2026; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026W/AIMS/papers/Budhkar_The_Deployment_Gap_in_AI_Media_Detection_Platform-Aware_and_Visually_CVPRW_2026_paper.pdf): detectors with AUC ≈ 0.99 in clean settings suffer substantial degradation under platform-aware attacks with pronounced calibration collapse.

The convergence: the field exhibits roughly a two-orders-of-magnitude reality gap — 90–99% accuracy on academic benchmarks translates to 40–60% accuracy on real-world content, with the best commercial systems hovering around 80%.

---

## 8. Proactive Detection and Provenance

- **AdvMark** (IJCAI 2024; https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0673.pdf): fine-tunes robust watermarks into adversarial watermarks.
- **LampMark** (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.17209v1): training-free landmark perceptual watermarks.
- **ProMark** (CVPR 2024; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Asnani_ProMark_Proactive_Diffusion_Watermarking_for_Causal_Attribution_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf): embeds up to 2^16 unique watermarks into training data.
- **ZoDiac** (NeurIPS 2024; https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/43d33182360378d5c8e69dd706c24f2f-Paper-Conference.pdf): Stable Diffusion latent space watermarking; >98% detection rate, <6.4% false-positive rate.
- **RAW** (NeurIPS 2024; https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/ee62ab636066cf45a27246acca9545b7-Paper-Conference.pdf): learnable watermarks with provable false-positive guarantees via conformal prediction.
- **C2PA Content Provenance** (https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/1.3/specs/C2PA_Specification.html): cryptographically signed manifests supported by major media/tech companies.

---

## 9. Ethical Concerns

1. **Non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII)**: A 10-country survey of 16,000+ respondents found 2.2% personal victimization and 1.8% perpetration rates even in jurisdictions with specific legislation (https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3613904.3642382).
2. **Election misinformation**: Recorded Future identified 82 deepfakes impersonating public figures (July 2023–July 2024) across 38 countries; 26.8% promoted scams, 25.6% fabricated misleading statements, 15.8% were electioneering (https://assets.recordedfuture.com/insikt-report-pdfs/2024/ta-2024-0924.pdf). A Knight First Amendment Institute analysis of 78 election deepfakes found non-AI "cheap fakes" were used seven times more often than AI content, but AI deepfakes pose disproportionate risks via the "liar's dividend" (https://knightcolumbia.org/blog/we-looked-at-78-election-deepfakes-political-misinformation-is-not-an-ai-problem).
3. **The liar's dividend**: Purdue's GRAIL lab documents politicians dismissing real evidence as AI-generated (https://www.brookings.edu/articles/watch-out-for-false-claims-of-deepfakes-and-actual-deepfakes-this-election-year/).
4. **Demographic bias**: A large-scale annotation study with 47 attributes and 65M+ labels found detection backbones are strongly affected by age, gender, ethnicity, and other attributes (IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society, 2024; https://doi.org/10.1109/tts.2024.3365421). Several SOTA detectors show higher accuracy for lighter skin tones (Ju et al., WACV 2024; https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/WACV2024/papers/Ju_Improving_Fairness_in_Deepfake_Detection_WACV_2024_paper.pdf). However, a 2026 study testing modern pretrained checkpoints across demographics found no systematic bias within small statistical margins (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3796544).
5. **Evidentiary reliability**: The "Deepfake Mom" case illustrates that without validated reliability schemes, detection outputs cannot support accusations in court (https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3699710).
6. **Privacy in detection systems**: FL work addresses the tension between centralized training (better accuracy) and decentralized training (GDPR compliance).
7. **Dual-use concerns**: Detection algorithms provide direct feedback to generation algorithms about what makes deepfakes detectable (https://arxiv.org/html/2407.06174v3).

---

## 10. Regulatory Frameworks

### 10.1 European Union — AI Act
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (https://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj) was adopted on 13 June 2024.
- **Article 50(4)**: Deployers of deepfake-generating AI systems must disclose that content has been artificially generated or manipulated, with exceptions for authorized law enforcement or for artistic/creative/satirical/fictional works where disclosure is limited to indicating synthetic content existence.
- **Article 50(2)**: Providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video, or text must mark outputs in a machine-readable format.
- **Article 50(5)**: Information must be provided "in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure."
- **Recital 134**: Disclosure obligation is "limited to disclosure of the existence of such generated or manipulated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work."
- **Effective dates**: Article 50 applies from **2 August 2026** (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/guidelines-ai-transparency-obligations).
- **Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content**: voluntary code by independent experts through the AI Office addressing provider marking/detection and deployer labeling.

The **Digital Services Act** requires VLOPs to identify, assess, and mitigate systemic risks including malicious deepfakes. The **Directive on Combating Violence Against Women** must be transposed by June 14, 2027, criminalizing production and sharing of sexually explicit deepfakes without consent.

### 10.2 United States
**TAKE IT DOWN Act** (Pub. L. 119-12; https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/146):
- Passed Senate unanimous consent (13 February 2025) and House 409-2 (28 April 2025); signed 19 May 2025.
- Amends Section 223 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 223) to criminalize intentional disclosure of non-consensual intimate visual depictions, including "digital forgeries" defined as any intimate visual depiction "created through the use of software, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or any other computer-generated or technological means."
- **Penalties**: Up to 2 years' imprisonment (3 years when depicting a minor), plus fines and mandatory restitution.
- **Section 3**: Requires covered platforms to establish notice-and-removal process within one year (by 19 May 2026) and remove flagged content within 48 hours of valid notice.

**State legislation**: Between 46 and 47 states have enacted deepfake laws since 2019/2022, with ~170 laws total and 146+ bills introduced in 2025 alone (Panels 1 and 4 cite slightly different counts: 46 states vs. 47 states). Major examples:
- **California AB 2655 (2024)**: requires large platforms to block materially deceptive digitally modified election content during specified periods.
- **Arizona HB 2394 (2024)**: grants citizens right to bring legal actions for digital impersonation without consent.
- **Texas Election Code § 255.004** (2019): criminalizes deepfake videos within 30 days of election.
- **Tennessee ELVIS Act**: first state law explicitly protecting voice as a right of publicity in AI context.
- **17 states** have enacted laws specifically addressing deepfake-based intimidation, bullying, and harassment (https://www.ncsl.org/technology-and-communication/deceptive-audio-or-visual-media-deepfakes-2024-legislation).

The FCC has also banned AI-generated voices in robocalls (https://www.brookings.edu/articles/watch-out-for-false-claims-of-deepfakes-and-actual-deepfakes-this-election-year/).

### 10.3 China
**Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis of Internet-based Information Services** (Order No. 12; https://www.cac.gov.cn/2022-12/11/c_1672221949318230.htm). Adopted by CAC, MIIT, and Ministry of Public Security on 25 November 2022; effective 10 January 2023:
- **Article 6**: Prohibits use of deep-synthesis services to produce or disseminate prohibited information or fabricate false news.
- **Article 9**: Mandatory real-identity authentication of users.
- **Article 10**: Content moderation via technical or manual review.
- **Article 11**: Mandatory rumor-refutation mechanism.
- **Articles 14–15**: Training-data management; safety assessments for biometric-feature tools.
- **Articles 16–17**: Mandatory visible marking for content that "may lead to public confusion or misidentification." Article 18 makes deletion/alteration of marks illegal.
- **Articles 19–20**: Mandatory algorithm filing for services with opinion-forming or social-mobilization capabilities.

**Companion**: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15; effective 15 August 2023; https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10666/202308/content_6900864.html) cross-references the Deep Synthesis Provisions for content marking.

### 10.4 United Kingdom and International
- **UK Online Safety Act 2023**: criminalizes sharing/threatening to share intimate images without consent (6-month sentence; up to 2 years for intent to distress). **Criminal Justice Bill (2024)** criminalizes creation of sexually explicit deepfakes without consent, even without intent to share (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/government-crackdown-on-deepfakes-creation).
- **South Korea**: 2024–2025 amendments to Information and Communications Network Act require explicit labeling of AI-generated content.
- **Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI** (opened September 2024; not yet in force): transparency and risk management obligations.
- **OECD AI Principles** (updated 2024): intergovernmental AI standard.
- **G7 Hiroshima AI Process** (2023): guiding principles and code of conduct for advanced AI systems.

---

## 11. Quantitative Summary

| Task | Best in-dataset (academic) | Best real-world | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image deepfake detection | AUC ~0.95–0.99 (UFD, NPR on academic datasets) | AUC ~0.52–0.56 on DF-Eval-2024; best commercial ~0.82 accuracy | ~40–50% AUC |
| Audio deepfake detection | EER ~0.5–2% on ASVspoof 2019 LA; ASVspoof 5 best minDCF 0.266 closed | AUC 0.43–0.58 on DF-Eval-2024; AASIST in-the-wild 24.73% EER | ~50% AUC drop |
| Video deepfake detection | AUC 0.95–0.99 on FF++ | AUC 0.50–0.63 on DF-Eval-2024; best commercial ~82% accuracy | ~30–50% AUC drop |

Cross-dataset generalization gaps within academic benchmarks: ~11–15% AUC decline for transformer-based and CNN-based detectors.

---

## 12. Conclusion

Since 2022, deepfake detection has matured in architectural sophistication — transformer-based, CLIP-adapted, audio-visual, articulatory, and foundation-model approaches have collectively raised in-domain performance to saturation (>95% AUC on standard benchmarks). Three persistent realities define the current state:

1. **The deployment gap**: Models near-perfect on academic datasets perform near chance on real-world content (Deepfake-Eval-2024: 45–57% AUC drops). Closing this requires broader and more current training corpora and platform-aware adversarial robustness testing.

2. **The architectural plateau**: Empirical evidence suggests training-data diversity drives generalization more than model size or attention mechanism. Foundation-model adaptation with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (0.03–0.08% of parameters) and federated/privacy-preserving training have emerged as the most promising directions.

3. **The regulatory momentum**: The EU AI Act (effective August 2026 for Article 50), US TAKE IT DOWN Act (May 2025; enforcement by May 2026), and China's Deep Synthesis Provisions (effective January 2023) together establish a global baseline of disclosure-and-labeling obligations, positioning detection and watermarking as compliance infrastructure.

Unresolved challenges include cross-generator generalization to unseen diffusion architectures, robustness to compression and platform transformations, federated on-device deployment under privacy constraints, harmonized provenance standards (C2PA, watermarking), and detection under deliberate adversarial countermeasures. Researchers increasingly frame deepfake detection not as a forensic arms race but as a socio-technical system in which detection, provenance, regulation, and media literacy operate together.

# Adaptive Input Systems for Musicians with Hand Tremor in DAW Environments: A Research Synthesis

## 1. Premise corrections the evidence base requires

Before any comparison is possible, three of the brief's central premises must be flagged because the documentation does not support them.

**Ableton Live does not ship a "MIDI velocity smoothing" tremor feature.** Live's Velocity MIDI effect (Live 12 manual §30.8) is a memoryless per-note remap with three out-of-range modes — Clip, Gate, and Fixed — plus a Random control. It cannot smooth temporal jitter because it has no time window, no averaging, no median filter, and no rise/fall parameter (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-midi-effect-reference/; https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/; https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/midi-tools/). The only literal "smoothing" inside Live is in Max for Live modulators, which acts on modulation curves, not note velocity (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/max-for-live-devices/). Forum users do use Gate mode as a workaround — "use gate mode in the Velocity device, and set the 'lowest' slider to 25, 30, etc. basically adjust it til it no longer picks up the quiet notes" (https://forum.ableton.com/viewtopic.php?t=120139) — but this is a user workaround, not a productized feature. Live 12's accessibility work is vision-first (screen reader support, Tab navigation, high-contrast theme; https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/accessibility-options-in-live/).

**Logic Pro's Smart Controls contain no tremor compensation.** Apple's documentation describes them only as on-screen macros that "change one or more parameters for the track's channel strip, instrument, and effect plug-ins" (https://support.apple.com/guide/logicpro/smart-controls-overview-lgcp7e59f24b/mac). The Logic Pro 2024 Accessibility Conformance (VPAT) report lists only generic motor accommodations: Sticky Keys, Slow Keys, Mouse Keys, Switch Control, and VoiceOver (https://support.apple.com/content/dam/edam/edam/applecare/images/en_US/otherassets/accessibility/vpat_logic_pro_2024.pdf). The "Tremolo" and "Vibrato" parameters in Logic are audio effects, not input filters (https://help.apple.com/pdf/logicpromac-effects/en_US/logic-pro-mac-effects-user-guide.pdf). A doctoral project at the Università degli Studi di Milano documents an artisanal accessibility setup using Logic Pro + Max + an eye tracker + micro-muscular sensors, but this is research, not a shipping feature (https://air.unimi.it/retrieve/a7a83c36-2310-4105-b143-57edcab7f0f8/phd_unimi_R13911_3.pdf).

**SteadyMouse is the only genuine tremor filter in the set, but it filters mouse pointers, not MIDI.** SteadyMouse 2 (manual Jan 2026; https://www.steadymouse.com/manual/) sits at the OS cursor layer and is transparent to all applications — including any DAW — but has no knowledge of MIDI semantics. Its seven filter sets (Allegro, Feather, Adagio, Classic, Artistry, Laggy, Steadicam) and a filter-strength slider with the documented tuning procedure ("Start with mouse speed below ten percent and filter strength around 95%… then decrease strength until tremor just begins to reappear") trade latency for tremor cancellation. It auto-disables Windows "Enhanced Pointer Precision" because it "actually degrades precision." It is Windows-only; a Mac port is acknowledged as "extremely difficult" (https://www.steadymouse.com/manual/; https://www.steadymouse.com/about/).

**Structural consequence:** the three filtering layers are disjoint. A MIDI keyboard performance with tremor-contaminated velocities, duplicated triggers, and wobbly pitch-bend bypasses SteadyMouse entirely, because SteadyMouse filters cursor/button events, not MIDI streams. Conversely, Live's Velocity device and Logic's parameter mapping graphs touch MIDI data but are blind to gesture frequency. Intentional vibrato in DAW practice (pitch-bend CC, aftertouch, mouse-drawn automation) lives in no filter's default path. **No commercially documented DAW feature performs frequency-selective separation of pathological tremor from expressive gesture at the MIDI layer.**

---

## 2. The core signal problem: pathological tremor and vibrato occupy the same band

The clinical and acoustic literature documents the following ranges:

| Signal | Frequency | Source |
|---|---|---|
| PD rest tremor | 4–6 Hz (some 3–6 Hz) | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573102/; https://parkinsons.org/symptoms/tremor; https://www.racgp.org.au/getattachment/4b03a304-f3a5-4571-917f-ee52f594808e/Classification-and-treatment-of-tremor.aspx |
| Essential tremor (action/postural) | 4–12 Hz | https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2021.684835/full; https://publications.ri.cmu.edu/storage/publications/pub_files/pub3/riviere_cameron_1995_2/riviere_cameron_1995_2.pdf |
| ET at rest (EMG) | 5–8 Hz | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573102/ |
| Enhanced physiological tremor | 6–12 Hz | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573102/ |
| Western lyric vocal vibrato | 5–8 Hz, extent < ±1.0 semitone (≈ ±6%), sinusoidal | https://pubs.aip.org/asa/jasa/article/130/1/EL1/907816 |
| Violin/cello vibrato | 4–10 Hz, means 5.5–6.63 Hz | https://exa.ai/library/publication/ddgkqcy2fr5 |
| Task-specific bowing tremor in violinists | 4.7–6.7 Hz; wrist flexion-extension; onset ~43 years | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4053556/; https://tremorjournal.org/articles/10.5334/tohm.187 |
| Secondary task-specific bowing tremor post-temporal-lobectomy | ~7 Hz, right-arm-only | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4117185/ |
| 23-musician TSTM study | 6.5 ± 0.9 Hz; onset 44.6 ± 13.6 years, 35.1 ± 13.5 years after starting instrument | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4677731/ |
| Pathological tremor band (general) | 3–15 Hz | http://www.neuralrehabilitation.org/projects/tremor/Documents/deliverables/TREMOR%20D4.1%20update.pdf |

**Overlap arithmetic:** vibrato at 5–8 Hz lies 100% inside the 4–12 Hz ET band (intersection = 5–8 Hz = 3 Hz of the 8 Hz ET band, i.e., 37.5% of ET). PD rest tremor at 4–6 Hz overlaps vibrato at 5–6 Hz = 1 Hz = 33% of vibrato, 50% of PD rest. The EMG-measured ET-at-rest band of 5–8 Hz is *identical* to the vocal vibrato band. A Brazilian clinical comparison found PD mean frequency 5.29 ± 1.18 Hz and ET 5.97 ± 1.1 Hz, and concluded that "tremor analysis alone using the methodology described here is not sufficient to differentiate tremor in ET and PD" (https://www.scielo.br/anp/a/FNMcgRcwCDZgzgfCc3qPLwn/?lang=en). The discriminators the literature actually relies on are *regularity, sinusoidal shape, and context* — not rate. A vocal case study of one person with both vibrato and essential voice tremor found sung modulation was slower, more prominent, and *more regular* than pathological tremor, "suggesting differences in the neural bases" (https://exa.ai/library/publication/3fjs73lrd3d). A frequency-domain filter therefore cannot separate them.

A second piece of physiological evidence tightens the constraint: after a violin vibrato run stops, persisting EMG rhythmic groups *accelerate into the 8–12 Hz physiological tremor range*, showing vibrato is built on the same oscillatory machinery as tremor.
